value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1
variable_description: How much school the child had missed since the start of the school year, banded, as the teacher reported it on the AvEDI. The dictionary defines the item as a "Variable to indicate how many days the child has been absent from school since the beginning of the school year", asked as "How many days has this child been absent since the start of the year". A1A to A1D on the same row split that absence by reason but are yes-or-no flags, not a decomposition of the band. A1 is not one of the items the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, so it never enters the PHYS score.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1
value_definition: A single-digit integer in four bands: 1 for 0 to 1 day, 2 for 2 to 5 days, 3 for 6 to 10 days, 4 for greater than 10 days. The entry publishes no missing-data codes, and its one-character field format leaves no room for the 88 and 99 conventions the dictionary applies to the wider AvEDI item set.
limitation: It cannot give a day count, and its lowest band merges a child who never missed a day with one who missed a single day; A1Z, present only from the 2018 cycle, is the item that separates them. Absence is also counted up to the day the teacher completed the instrument rather than over a full school year, so a child assessed in May and a child assessed in November are not on the same denominator.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary carries a full entry for A1 with the data element description, the instrument wording and the four-band code frame, and its section 7.1 table lists the items allocated to each domain, which excludes A1.
evidence_quote: Variable to indicate how many days the child has been absent from school since the beginning of the school year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's wording 'Days absent since the start of the year' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both value definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that the field is banded or that it does not feed a domain score.

variable_description: Whether the child can manage the toilet on their own most of the time, in the teacher's judgement. The instrument asks "Would you say this child is independent in toileting habits most of the time", and the dictionary counts the item towards the physical health and wellbeing domain score. It is coded the opposite way round to A2, A3 and A4: here the higher code, 2, is the positive answer.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A5
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know, so the direction is reversed relative to the yes-first items earlier in section A.
limitation: It is a judgement about classroom independence, not a clinical statement about continence, and the qualifier 'most of the time' means an occasional accident does not move the answer. The AEDC also does not compute domain categories for children diagnosed with special needs, so this item cannot be used to profile the children for whom toileting support is most likely to be an issue.
rationale: The dictionary's A5 entry gives the description, purpose, instrument wording and the reversed code frame, section 7.1 lists A5 as a physical health and wellbeing item, and section 3.1 states that domain categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is independent in toileting habits most of the time
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Washroom' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so a reader had neither the question nor the reversed coding, which is where the mistake happens.

value_domain: AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)

variable_description: Whether the child has settled on one hand rather than swapping, in the teacher's judgement. The instrument asks "Would you say this child shows an established hand preference (right vs. left or vice versa)", so the answer is about whether a preference exists, not which hand it is. It is one of the twelve items the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, where an established preference is treated as a marker of fine motor development.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A6
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It cannot identify left-handed children: both a left-handed and a right-handed child answer yes, and the AvEDI collects no column recording which hand. A no also confounds genuine ambidexterity with a child the teacher has simply not watched closely enough, which is otherwise the 88 category.
rationale: The dictionary's A6 entry gives the instrument wording, which names both hands as equivalent affirmative cases, along with the code frame, and section 7.1 lists A6 as a physical health and wellbeing item.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child shows an established hand preference (right vs. left or vice versa)
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Hand preference' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which invites the reader to expect a left-or-right code that the column does not carry.

value_domain: AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)

variable_description: Whether the child moves around without bumping into or tripping over things, in the teacher's judgement. The instrument spells the criterion out: "Would you say this child is well co-ordinated (i.e. moves without running into or tripping over things)?". It is the gross motor counterpart to A8 and A9, which rate pen grip and object handling, and all three feed the physical health and wellbeing domain score.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A7
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know, in the same direction as A5, A6 and the B-series literacy items.
limitation: It is a single yes-or-no on whole-body movement, so it cannot grade coordination or separate a mild clumsiness from a motor impairment; the three-point items A10 and A12 are the nearest thing to a gradient. A yes also does not mean the child was assessed under comparable conditions, since teachers observe children in very different play spaces.
rationale: The dictionary's A7 entry publishes the instrument wording with its parenthetical criterion and the code frame, and section 7.1 lists A7 among the physical health and wellbeing domain items.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is well co-ordinated (i.e. moves without running into or tripping over things)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Well coordinated' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without the criterion the teacher was actually asked to apply.

value_domain: AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A8
variable_description: The teacher's rating of how well the child holds a pen, crayon or brush. The dictionary gives the purpose as "To rate how well the child holds a pen, crayon or brush", and unlike the yes-or-no items earlier in section A this one is graded on three levels. It is a fine motor item in the physical health and wellbeing domain, and the closest physical companion to the writing items B18 to B23 in the language and cognitive domain.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A8
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know. Both ends of the scale carry a merged label, code 1 covering poor and very poor and code 3 covering good and very good, so the extremes cannot be separated.
limitation: It cannot separate a grip problem from a lack of practice, since a child who has rarely held a pencil and a child with a motor difficulty both rate poor. The merged top and bottom categories also mean the column cannot identify the very poorest or very best writers, which matters if the intent is to find children needing occupational therapy referral.
rationale: The dictionary's A8 entry gives the instrument wording, the purpose and the three-point code frame with its merged end labels and the don't-know convention, and section 7.1 lists A8 as a physical health and wellbeing item.
evidence_quote: How would you rate this child's proficiency at holding a pen, crayon or brush
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Proficient at holding pen' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no idea that the response is a three-point rating with merged extremes.

value_domain: AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A9
variable_description: The teacher's rating of how well the child handles objects, on the same three-point scale as A8, A10, A11, A12 and A13. The instrument asks "How would you rate this child's ability to manipulate objects" without naming particular objects, so the teacher applies it to whatever the classroom offers. It is one of the fine motor items in the physical health and wellbeing domain.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A9
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know.
limitation: The question names no task, so the rating is anchored to the materials and expectations of one classroom rather than to a fixed standard, which makes it weaker for comparing individual children than for comparing large groups. It also overlaps heavily with A8, so treating the two as independent evidence of fine motor skill double counts one judgement.
rationale: The dictionary's A9 entry publishes the instrument wording, the purpose and the three-point code frame, and section 7.1 lists A9 among the physical health and wellbeing domain items.
evidence_quote: How would you rate this child's ability to manipulate objects
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Manipulates objects' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice and did not say the response is a graded rating.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AGCampusID
variable_description: The Commonwealth's own code for the school campus at which the child was assessed. The dictionary defines it as "The individual campus code used by the Australian Government to identify each school campus participating in the AEDC", held on the Master Unit Record File and "Suppressed for schools outside of a data recipient's jurisdiction". It appears in PLIDA only on the 2018 cycle table, because the dictionary records the item being replaced by AGLocationID from 2021 and fully discontinued in 2024.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AGCampusID
value_definition: A five-digit integer allocated by the Australian Government, not a serial within the AEDC file, so the value range is set by the national school register rather than by this collection.
limitation: It cannot follow a school across cycles in PLIDA, since only the 2018 table carries it and its successors sit under different names; SCHOOLID is the identifier present in every cycle. It also identifies a campus, not a school or a teacher, so a multi-campus school splits across values while TEACHERID separates classes within a campus.
rationale: The dictionary's AGCampusID entry gives the definition, the five-digit format, the Master URF availability, the jurisdictional suppression rule and the 2021 replacement and 2024 discontinuation, which together explain why it appears in one PLIDA cycle only.
evidence_quote: The individual campus code used by the Australian Government to identify each school campus participating in the AEDC.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'National campus identifier used by deewr' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the identifier is suppressed outside a recipient's jurisdiction or that it lives on only one cycle.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCat
variable_description: The finest published banding of the child's age, in steps of roughly three months across the school-entry range. It is a derived variable, built from the age the dictionary describes as "based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher". AGECUT, AGEGROUP and AGEGROUP3TO7 on the same row are coarser cuts of the same underlying age, and AGEINMONTHS is the ungrouped version.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCat
value_definition: A two-digit integer from 0 to 15, so sixteen codes despite the name; the '15 narrow' in the custodian's label counts the non-zero codes. Codes 1 to 13 step in roughly three-month intervals from 3 years 8 months to 6 years 10 months; code 0 is everything under 3 years 8 months, code 14 spans 6 years 10 months to 7 years 6 months, and code 15 is everything above.
limitation: The bands are not equal width, so treating the code as a linear age scale compresses the middle and stretches both tails, and a regression on the raw code will not recover a per-month effect. Age is also measured at the day the teacher completed the instrument rather than at a fixed census date, so two children on the same code were assessed at different points in the school year.
rationale: The dictionary's AgeCat entry publishes all sixteen bands with their exact year-and-month boundaries and marks the variable as derived, and section 4.4 states how AEDC age is constructed.
evidence_quote: AEDC age is based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Age categories (15 narrow)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, giving neither the number of codes nor the fact that the bands are uneven at both ends.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCut
variable_description: The coarsest numeric grouping of the child's age, splitting the cohort into under five, five, and six or older. The dictionary marks it as derived and gives its purpose as "A grouping variable for child age", which is what it is normally used for: a control or a cross-tabulation axis when the sixteen bands of AGECAT are too fine. AGEGROUP holds the same idea as text with the top group cut at seven rather than six.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCut
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three codes: 0 for under 5 years, 1 for 5 years and 2 for 6 years and older.
limitation: Its top and bottom categories are open, so a four-year-old and a three-year-old share code 0 while a six-year-old and an eight-year-old share code 2, which hides exactly the age spread that matters when comparing schools with different entry rules. The bottom category also mixes children the AEDC excludes from domain categories, those under four years, with four-year-olds who are scored.
rationale: The dictionary's AgeCut entry gives the purpose, the derived source and the three-code frame, and section 3.1 records that domain categories are not calculated for children less than four years of age.
evidence_quote: Domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs, or children less than four years of age.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Age categories (3 broad)' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without the cut points or the interaction with the under-four exclusion.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup
variable_description: The confidentialised age grouping the AEDC uses in its published outputs, held as text rather than as a code. Section 4.4 of the dictionary says the age variable is "available in years and is confidentialised as follows" and then lists under five years, five years, six years and over six years, and this is the column that carries that grouping. AGECUT expresses almost the same split numerically, but its top band starts at six while this one holds six-year-olds separately and reserves its top value for seven and over.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup
value_definition: A two-character text field with four values: '<5' for under 5 years, '5' for 5 to under 6, '6' for 6 to under 7, and '>6' for 7 years and over. The field is left justified, not numeric.
limitation: Two of its four values are not numbers, so converting the column to numeric silently drops the youngest and oldest children to missing and leaves an apparently clean five-and-six-year-old sample that is missing its tails. The label '>6' is also misleading on its own, since the dictionary defines it as age 7 years or more rather than anything above six.
rationale: The dictionary's AgeGroup entry gives the four text values with their exact age boundaries and records the field as text with left justification, and section 4.4 states the confidentialisation rule the grouping implements.
evidence_quote: This variable is available in years and is confidentialised as follows:
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Age group' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not warn that the column is text or that '>6' means seven and over.

value_domain: AEDC age in completed years, top coded at 7
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup3to7
variable_description: The child's age in completed years at the time the teacher filled in the instrument, held as a plain integer from 3 to 7. It is the numeric age variable most convenient for analysis on the AEDC core tables, and the dictionary marks it as derived rather than reported. AGEINMONTHS is the finer version of the same quantity, AGECAT the finer banding, and AGEGROUP the text grouping used for publication.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup3to7
value_definition: A single-digit integer taking 3 for age 3 to under 4, 4 for 4 to under 5, 5 for 5 to under 6, 6 for 6 to under 7, and 7 for 7 and over. Only the top code is open; the others are exact one-year intervals.
limitation: Its name suggests a range of three to seven, but code 7 is a top code with no upper bound, so an eight-year-old repeating a year is indistinguishable from a child who has just turned seven. Rounding down to completed years also loses up to eleven months of development, which is large relative to the age effects the AEDC domain cut-offs are designed to absorb.
rationale: The dictionary's AgeGroup3to7 entry publishes the five codes with their exact age intervals and marks the source as derived, and section 4.4 states that AEDC age is built from date of birth against the instrument completion date.
evidence_quote: Age >= 7
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Age in years' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that 7 is a top code rather than an exact age.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeInMonths
variable_description: The child's age in whole months when the teacher completed the instrument, and the finest age measure on the AEDC file. The dictionary marks it as derived and section 4.4 explains the derivation: "AEDC age is based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher." Every other age column on the row, AGECAT, AGECUT, AGEGROUP and AGEGROUP3TO7, is a banding of this quantity.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeInMonths
value_definition: A three-digit integer counting completed months, so a child of five years and three months is 63. There is no code frame; the domain is open across the school-entry age range.
limitation: It is age at assessment, not age at a common reference date, so it moves with when in the school year the teacher happened to complete the instrument as much as with the child's date of birth; MOC, the month of completion, is the column needed to adjust for that. It also cannot be turned back into a date of birth, which is not released.
rationale: The dictionary's AgeInMonths entry gives the derived source and the three-digit integer format, and section 4.4 states the derivation from reported date of birth against the instrument completion date.
evidence_quote: AEDC age is based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Age in months' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what the age is measured against, which is the whole difficulty with the column.

value_domain: Year of first arrival in Australia (four-digit year, 9999 unknown)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ArrivalYear
variable_description: The year the child first came to Australia, asked on the instrument as "In which year did the child first arrive in Australia". Read against AGEINMONTHS it gives an approximate age at migration, and against COUNTRY and PLACEOFBIRTH on the same row it distinguishes a child born overseas who arrived as an infant from one who arrived shortly before starting school. The dictionary records the item as introduced in 2015, which is why it is absent from the 2009 and 2012 cycle tables.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ArrivalYear
value_definition: A four-digit integer holding a calendar year, with 9999 reserved for unknown. There is no separate not-applicable code for children born in Australia.
limitation: The 9999 sentinel is a valid four-digit year to any arithmetic, so a mean or a difference computed without excluding it is badly wrong. It also records the first arrival, so a child who left and returned is dated by the earlier trip, and it says nothing about visa status or whether the family arrived together.
rationale: The dictionary's ArrivalYear entry gives the definition, the instrument wording, the four-digit format with 9999 for unknown, and the 2015 introduction, matching the cycles on which the column appears in PLIDA.
evidence_quote: In which year did the child first arrive in Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Year of arrival' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not disclose the 9999 sentinel, which is the practical trap in the column.

value_domain: Indigenous status (Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSI
variable_description: Whether the child is recorded as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, the gate on every other item in the AEDC Indigenous table. The dictionary defines it as follows: "A child is considered to be 'Indigenous' if he or she identifies as being of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin. The term 'origin' is considered to relate to people's Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent and for some, but not all, their cultural identity." ATSITYPE beside it splits Aboriginal from Torres Strait Islander origin, and B1A to B1D rate the child's use of Aboriginal English, Kriol and traditional languages.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSI
value_definition: A single-digit integer, documented by the AEDC as 0 for no and 1 for yes. The PLIDA data item list describes the field differently, as 1 for Indigenous with null signifying non-Indigenous or non-identifying, so the negative case may arrive as missing rather than as zero.
limitation: The two published descriptions disagree on how a non-Indigenous child is stored, so a test written as ATSI equals 0 can return nobody while ATSI equals 1 works; check the observed values before building a denominator. The item is also a school enrolment record of origin rather than a self-report by the child or family at census time, and 'not identifying' is indistinguishable from 'not Indigenous' in either coding.
rationale: The dictionary's ATSI entry carries the full origin definition, the instrument wording and the two-value code frame, and the PLIDA data item list for the same column states a different missing convention, which is the discrepancy a user has to resolve.
evidence_quote: A child is considered to be 'Indigenous' if he or she identifies as being of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the PLIDA wording about nulls and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without the AEDC's own definition of origin or any note that the two sources describe the coding differently.

value_domain: Indigenous origin type (Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, both, neither, not stated)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSIType
variable_description: Which Indigenous origin the child is recorded as having, asked only where ATSI on the same row is yes. The dictionary states the filter as "Only answer if ATSI = Yes" and the jurisdictional rule as "Not provided in New South Wales", with a 2015 filter revision noting that previous cycles did not include NSW students at all. Its purpose is to add detail rather than to change the count of Indigenous children, which ATSI alone establishes.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSIType
value_definition: A single-digit integer with five codes: 1 Aboriginal but not Torres Strait Islander origin, 2 Torres Strait Islander but not Aboriginal origin, 3 both, 4 neither, and 9 not stated or unknown. The 2012 cycle revised these field values.
limitation: Its blanks are dominated by the filter and by New South Wales, so a national split of Aboriginal against Torres Strait Islander children taken from this column omits the largest jurisdiction and is not comparable across cycles. Code 4, neither origin, can also appear on rows where ATSI is yes, so the two columns can contradict each other and ATSI should be the one used to define the population.
rationale: The dictionary's ATSIType entry gives the purpose, the instrument wording, the five-code frame, the conditional filter on ATSI, the New South Wales exclusion and the 2012 and 2015 revisions.
evidence_quote: Only answer if ATSI = Yes
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Indigenous background' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and never disclosed the filter, the New South Wales gap or the internally contradictory 'neither' code.

value_domain: AvEDI three-point proficiency rating with not-applicable (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88, 99)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B1
variable_description: The teacher's rating of how effectively the child uses English, asked as "How would you rate this child's ability to use language effectively in English". The dictionary allocates it to the communication skills and general knowledge domain, not to language and cognitive skills, so it feeds COMGEN rather than LANGCOG. B1A to B1D in the AEDC Indigenous table carry the parallel ratings for Aboriginal English, Kriol, traditional languages and other Indigenous languages, and ESL and LANG on the core table record whether English is the home language at all.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B1
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable. It is one of the few AvEDI items to carry the not-applicable code.
limitation: A low rating is not evidence of a language delay: the item rates English specifically, so a child fluent in another language and new to English scores at the bottom on linguistic competence they in fact have. Reading it alongside LBOTE, ESL and the B1A to B1D Indigenous language ratings is the only way to tell the two situations apart.
rationale: The dictionary's B1 entry gives the instrument wording and the five-value code frame, section 7.1 lists B1 under the communication skills and general knowledge domain, and the B1a entry establishes the parallel other-language items.
evidence_quote: How would you rate this child's ability to use language effectively in English
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Proficient in english' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say which domain the item feeds or that a low score can reflect language background rather than ability.

value_domain: AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B10
variable_description: Whether the child shows curiosity about printed material, asked as "Would you say this child is interested in reading (inquisitive/curious about the meaning of printed material)?". It is one of the twenty-six items, B8 to B33, that the dictionary allocates to the language and cognitive skills domain, and it sits at the disposition end of that set: B11 to B17 test what the child can actually do with letters and words. E7 on the core table records whether the child is read to at home.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B10
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know, so the higher code is the positive answer across the whole B10 to B19 block.
limitation: It rates an attitude the teacher infers from behaviour in class, so a child who is interested in books at home but reticent at school reads as a no; it is not a measure of reading ability, which B15 to B17 carry. The binary form also gives no gradient, so it cannot separate mild from strong interest.
rationale: The dictionary's B10 entry gives the instrument wording with its parenthetical criterion and the code frame, and section 7.1 lists B10 among the language and cognitive skills domain items.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is interested in reading (inquisitive/curious about the meaning of printed material)?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Interested in reading' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, giving neither the code direction nor the distinction from the reading skill items.

value_domain: AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B11
variable_description: Whether the child can name at least some letters of the alphabet, the first rung of the literacy ladder in the AvEDI. The instrument asks "Would you say this child is able to identify some letters of the alphabet", with no threshold on how many. It is a language and cognitive skills domain item and the base for B12, which asks whether the child can attach sounds to letters.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B11
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.
limitation: Because 'some' is undefined, the item saturates: most children in their first year of school answer yes, so it separates the very lowest group from everyone else and carries almost no information about the rest. It also does not distinguish recognising a letter shape from knowing its name or its sound.
rationale: The dictionary's B11 entry gives the instrument wording, which sets the threshold at 'some letters', along with the code frame, and section 7.1 lists B11 among the language and cognitive skills domain items.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is able to identify some letters of the alphabet
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Identifies letters' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not convey how low the threshold is.

value_domain: AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B12
variable_description: Whether the child can attach sounds to letters, the phonics step between recognising letters in B11 and reading words in B15. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify if the child is able to attach sounds to letters", asked of the teacher as a single yes-or-no judgement. It is one of the language and cognitive skills domain items and, with B13 on rhyming, one of the two phonological awareness questions in the instrument.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B12
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is the teacher's impression from ordinary classroom work rather than a phonics assessment, so it will track how much explicit phonics teaching the class has done as well as the child's own skill. Nothing in the column says how many letter-sound correspondences the child knows, so it cannot be used to rank children within the yes group.
rationale: The dictionary's B12 entry gives the data element description, the purpose, the instrument wording and the code frame, and section 7.1 lists B12 among the language and cognitive skills domain items.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is able to attach sounds to letters
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Sounds to letters' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no code frame and no placement in the literacy sequence.

value_domain: AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B13
variable_description: Whether the child notices that words rhyme, asked as "Would you say this child is showing awareness of rhyming words". Rhyme awareness is the oral side of early literacy, so this item and B12 on letter sounds are the two phonological questions in a block otherwise concerned with print. It counts towards the language and cognitive skills domain score.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B13
value_definition: A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.
limitation: Rhyme is language specific, so a child whose home language is not English can show the awareness in that language and still be rated no here, which is why B1, LBOTE and ESL belong in any interpretation of a low score. The wording asks only whether awareness is showing, not whether the child can produce rhymes, so a yes sets a low bar.

variable_description: Which of the six triennial AEDC collections the row belongs to, numbered 1 to 6 for 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024. The dictionary defines it simply as "The AEDC collection cycle". It is not interchangeable with YEAR: cycle 1 spans both 2009 and 2010, and the AEDC directs that "2010 data is excluded from all results except Community / Local Community level results". Grouping on this column is how a PLIDA user reproduces an AEDC published figure, since every AEDC report is organised by cycle.

rationale: The Cycle element page gives the definition and the one-digit format, table 1 maps each cycle number to its collection year, and section 2.3 states the 2009/2010 overlap and the exclusion rule.

variable_description: Whether the child has a physical disability and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning. The AEDC's purpose for the item is "To identify if the child has a physical disability that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom", and it is the first of nine condition items D1 to D9 the teacher answers for every child. The code frame carries its own history: code 3 is a plain yes used only in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, while codes 1 and 2 split that yes into affects learning and does not affect learning from 2015 onwards.

value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 no, 1 yes. The dictionary's instruction is "Only answer if SpecialNeeds = Yes", so the column is populated only for children whose teacher gave them special needs status, and one child can carry a 1 on several DIAGNOSIS columns at once.
limitation: It does not distinguish type, control or treatment. A child on an insulin pump and a child newly diagnosed and still stabilising are one code, and because the question is asked only of special needs children, a well-managed diabetic child with no special needs status is missing entirely.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary publishes a data element entry for Diagnosis9 giving the element description, the instrument wording, the SpecialNeeds routing condition, the year the code was introduced and the two-value code list, and its instrument-change appendices explain how the condition list was revised in 2015, 2018 and 2024.
evidence_quote: What medical diagnosis (or diagnoses) qualifies this child as Special Needs – Diabetes
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's condition label with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said the item is routed off SPECIALNEEDS, never gave the 0/1 codes, and never warned that the population asked is a small selected group.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1 and section 3.2 Summary Indicators
variable_description: Whether the child was developmentally vulnerable on one or more of the five AEDC domains, the headline AEDC result. The dictionary describes it as "Vulnerable - One or more domains" and notes that "Vulnerability Summary Indicators do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on", so it is derived from PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY beside it. Vulnerable means a domain category of 1, the 0 to 10th percentile band, cut against the 2009 baseline that is held fixed for every later cycle so that cycles can be compared.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1 and section 3.2 Summary Indicators
value_definition: A one-digit integer taking 0 or 1. There is no not-applicable code, so DV1FLAG beside it is what tells you whether a 0 is a real result.
limitation: A 0 does not mean the child was assessed and found not vulnerable. The dictionary states that domain indicator categories are not calculated for children with special needs status or children under four years of age, and those children still appear with DV1 of 0, so any rate computed over all rows is wrong. DV1 also says nothing about which domain or how far below the cut-off the child fell; LOWTOTAL and the five category columns carry that.
rationale: The dictionary defines the element, explains in section 3.2 how the summary indicators are built from the domain categories, and states the exclusions that make the raw column unsafe to average.
evidence_quote: Domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs, or children less than four years of age.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Vulnerable - one or more domains' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, giving no warning that the zeros include children who were never scored and no pointer to the denominator flag next to it.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1Flag and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
variable_description: Whether the child belongs in the denominator when a developmentally-vulnerable-on-one-or-more rate is calculated. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of DV1" and explains that the flag exists because, when the Canadian Early Development Instrument was adapted for Australia, "work was conducted to refine the denominator (i.e., valid cases) for these two indicators to maximise the number of cases with reportable data". A published AEDC rate is therefore the count of DV1 equal to 1 over the count of DV1FLAG equal to 1, not over every row in the file.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1Flag and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
value_definition: A one-digit integer taking 0 or 1, where 1 means the child's record supports a DV1 result.
limitation: It is not a quality flag for the record as a whole. A child excluded here can still have valid age, language, schooling and special needs entries, and DV2FLAG and OT5FLAG in the same table carry their own denominators, so the three summary indicators are not computed over identical populations and their rates cannot be differenced as if they were.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element entry and Appendix 3 explains why the flag was created and what refining the denominator was for, which is the fact that makes the column usable.
evidence_quote: Two new variables, DV1Flag and DV2Flag, were created in the dataset to define this information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Qualifies for the denominator of dv1' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it never said how to use the flag or that the other summary indicators have different denominators.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.2 Summary Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child fell in the lowest AEDC category on at least two of the five developmental domains, the headline measure the AEDC reports as developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains. It is built by counting how many of PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY equal 1, the 0 to 10th percentile band of the 2009 national baseline. The dictionary notes that summary indicators "do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on". DV2FLAG on the same row says whether the child counts in the denominator when the percentage is worked out.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.2 Summary Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes. It is derived rather than collected, and the dictionary publishes no separate code for children who fall outside the DV2 denominator.
limitation: It is not a count of vulnerable domains, so it cannot separate a child vulnerable on two domains from one vulnerable on all five; LOWTOTAL carries the count. A 0 also does not prove the child was assessed on all five domains, because children excluded from the denominator can read as 0, which is exactly why DV2FLAG exists.
rationale: The dictionary defines DV2 as the developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains summary indicator, and section 3.2 explains that the indicator is calculated from the count of vulnerable domains rather than from a score of its own.
evidence_quote: Vulnerability Summary Indicators do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's phrase 'Vulnerable - two or more domains' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said which domains were counted, against what cut-off, or that a companion denominator flag exists.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether this child belongs in the denominator when the percentage developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains is calculated. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains", which means a correct DV2 rate is the mean of DV2 over the rows where this flag is 1, not over all rows. It exists because children with a special needs diagnosis, children aged three and children with too few valid domain scores are excluded from AEDC vulnerability reporting.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes. Derived from the per-domain validity flags together with special needs status and age.
limitation: It says nothing about the child's development, so filtering on it selects a reporting population rather than a vulnerable one. It is also not interchangeable with the per-domain validity flags such as EMOTVALID: a child can hold a valid score on one domain and still fail to qualify for the DV2 denominator.
rationale: The dictionary publishes DV2Flag as a derived denominator qualification variable with a 0/1 value list, alongside the per-domain validity flags that describe the exclusions it is built from.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording 'Qualifies for the denominator of dv2' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know that AEDC vulnerability rates must be computed over this flag rather than over every row.

value_domain: AEDC teacher-reported early intervention attendance (yes/no/don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E1
variable_description: The teacher's report of whether the child had attended an early intervention program before starting school, asked as "To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended an early intervention program". In the special needs table it sits with D1 to D10, the enduring problem flags for physical, sensory, speech, learning, emotional and behavioural difficulties, and with D11 which asks whether the child needs further assessment, so it is the service-use column beside a set of need columns. It is the closest thing the AEDC holds to a record of a child having received support before school entry.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E1
value_definition: A two-digit integer: 0 for no, 1 for yes and 88 for the standard AEDC don't-know code.
limitation: It names no program, no provider, no age at entry and no duration, so it cannot distinguish a single speech pathology block from three years of intensive support. Because the answer is the teacher's, 88 records only that the teacher did not know, and a 0 can mean the teacher was unaware rather than that no program was attended.
rationale: The dictionary gives E1 as an instrument item with its exact question wording and a three-value code list, and the registry places it in the AEDC special needs table beside the D-series problem indicators.
evidence_quote: To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended an early intervention program
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Attended an early intervention program' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not record that the answer is a teacher's report or that 88 codes don't know.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2ay
variable_description: How many hours a week, on average, the child attended the preschool or kindergarten program reported in E2Y, banded around the fifteen-hour national benchmark. The dictionary states its purpose as "To identify if the child was in regular educational programs for the mandatory amount of time", so the three bands are less than fifteen hours, fifteen hours, and more than fifteen hours. It is only answered where E2Y records attendance, and E2BY on the same row says what kind of setting the program ran in.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2ay
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for less than 15 hours per week, 2 for 15 hours per week, 3 for more than 15 hours per week, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.
limitation: It records a weekly average, not how long the child stayed enrolled, so a child who attended fifteen hours a week for one term is indistinguishable from one who did so for the full year. The bands also carry no information about attendance actually taken up, only about the program the child was enrolled in.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the item wording, its 2018 introduction and the four-code band list, and the registry places it alongside E2Y and E2BY in the same core table.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child was in regular educational programs for the mandatory amount of time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question stem 'To the best of your knowledge did the child attend the preschool / kindergarten program on average:' with no completion, and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the answer categories were entirely missing.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by
variable_description: What kind of service delivered the preschool or kindergarten program the child attended in the year before school, separating a standalone preschool or kindergarten from a long day care centre. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "the organisational basis for the child's preschool / kindergarten", which is the distinction most Australian early childhood policy work needs, because the same entitlement is delivered through both service types. It is answered only where E2Y records attendance, and E2AY gives the hours.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for preschool or kindergarten, 2 for long day care centre, 3 for other, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.
limitation: It identifies a setting type, not a provider, a funding source or a governance arrangement, so it cannot separate a government preschool from an independent or community one. Code 3 is an undifferentiated catch-all, so mobile, occasional care and school-attached services cannot be told apart from one another.
rationale: The dictionary gives E2by's exact instrument text, its purpose and its four-code value list, and the registry shows it sitting beside E2Y and E2AY in the same table.
evidence_quote: In what kind of setting was the preschool / kindergarten program?
supersedes_rationale: The entry held only the question stem with no answer categories and the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that long day care is one of the coded settings.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y
variable_description: Whether the child attended a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. It is the gate for the rest of the preschool block: E2AY records the weekly hours and E2BY the setting, and both are answered only where this column records attendance. The dictionary describes it as the variable that identifies "if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school", and it was introduced in 2018 in place of the earlier E2 series of childcare and preschool items.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y
value_definition: A two-digit integer with three codes: 1 for yes, 2 for no, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in 2018.
limitation: The coding is 1 for yes and 2 for no, unlike most AEDC yes/no items which use 0 and 1, so treating this as a 0/1 dummy turns every non-attender into an attender. It also does not carry back to earlier cycles: before 2018 the same information came from a different set of items, so an unadjusted trend from 2009 is not comparable.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording, the 2018 introduction, the 1/2/88 code list, and the conditional instructions on the dependent E2ay and E2by items.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question stem alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it missed the unusual 1-for-yes, 2-for-no coding and the 2018 break in the series.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (long day care)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay
variable_description: Whether the child was in long day care on a regular basis in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the first of six parallel columns, E3AY to E3FY, that cover long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative, a nanny and any other person, each coded the same way. Version 8.0 of the dictionary corrected the instruction on all six, recording that they are "asked to All" rather than only to children whose E2Y records a preschool program.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: No is coded 4, not 0, so a naive greater-than-zero test counts every non-attender as attending. Long day care here also overlaps with E2Y, because a long day care centre can deliver the preschool program reported there, so adding the E3 columns and E2Y together double counts the same child.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the five-code list and the version 8.0 correction to the filter, and the registry shows the six E3 columns sitting together in the same core table.
evidence_quote: E3ay – E3fy –correction to instruction, removed "only answer if E2y=yes" as these items are asked to All.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long question stem ending in 'long day care' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not show that 4 means no or that the filter was corrected in 2025.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (family day care)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by
variable_description: Whether the child was regularly in family day care in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. Family day care is the regulated home-based service, so this column separates it from the centre-based care in E3AY and from the informal relative care in E3CY and E3DY. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school", and the 2018 cycle rebuilt it from the earlier E2e and E2etime pair.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: The full-time and part-time split is the only intensity information available, so it cannot yield hours, days per week or weeks of the year. Code 3 is a real answer rather than a missing value, and dropping it as missing biases any full-time share upwards.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the derivation from E2e and E2etime in 2018, and the five-code value list for this specific care type.
evidence_quote: To identify how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry held the shared question stem ending in 'family day care' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the five sibling columns or explained the intensity codes.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy
variable_description: Whether a grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. This is the largest of the informal care categories in Australia and the reason the E3 block distinguishes grandparents from other relatives, who are captured separately in E3DY. Because the columns are a multiple response set, a child can be recorded here and in the formal care columns E3AY and E3BY at the same time.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It does not say whether the grandparent lived with the child, was paid, or was the child's primary carer, so it cannot identify kinship care arrangements or grandparent-headed households. The teacher is answering about a household arrangement they did not observe, so the don't-know rate is a property of teacher knowledge rather than of the family.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code list for the grandparent element of the non-parental care question, and the registry shows the six-column multiple response block in one table.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with a Grandparent in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'grandparent' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record the intensity codes or that the six columns are a multiple response set.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy
variable_description: Whether a relative other than a parent or grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the residual family category in the E3 block: grandparents are taken out into E3CY, and unrelated carers fall to E3EY for a nanny or E3FY for a friend or neighbour. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school".
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: The relationship itself is not recorded, so an aunt, an adult sibling and a cousin all collapse into one code and no family structure can be reconstructed from it. It also cannot be read as a measure of family support, since a family with no relative nearby and a family that declined help both record 4.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code value list for the other relative element of the non-parental care question, and names the 2018 derivation from E2g and E2gtime.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry held the shared question stem ending in 'other relative' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving the codes and the boundary against E3CY undocumented.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey
variable_description: Whether a nanny regularly cared for the child in the home in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the paid, unregulated, in-home category of the E3 block, distinct from the regulated home-based service captured in E3BY as family day care. Version 7.0 of the dictionary lists a correction to the field format and field values across E3ay to E3fy, so the published code list for this column is not identical in earlier dictionary releases.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It does not distinguish a live-in nanny from one who visits, or paid work from a reciprocal arrangement, so it cannot support any inference about household income. It is also a narrow category, so any subgroup estimate built on it should be checked against the AEDC suppression rules before it is reported.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the corrected five-code value list for the nanny element of the non-parental care question, and the version table records the field value correction covering E3ay to E3fy.
evidence_quote: Correction to field format/field values (PlaceOfBirth, B2-B7, C3-C51, E3ay-fy)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'nanny' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the published code list for this item had been corrected.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy
variable_description: Whether someone outside the family, such as a friend or a neighbour, regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It closes the E3 block as the catch-all: anything that was not long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative or a nanny lands here. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying care "with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school".
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: Being the residual category, it holds arrangements with nothing in common beyond not fitting the five named ones, so a positive value supports no statement about the type or quality of care. It is also the category a teacher is least likely to know about, so a low count here reflects reporting as much as behaviour.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code list for the other person element of the non-parental care question, and the registry shows it as the last of the six parallel columns.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'other (includes friend or neighbour)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so its role as the residual category and its code list were both missing.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4
variable_description: Whether the child attended a playgroup at any point in the years before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. Its reference window is deliberately wider than the rest of the E block: E2Y and the E3 columns ask about the single year before school, while this one asks about "the years before entering full time school". The dictionary records that it was introduced in the 2012 cycle and renamed from E3b in 2015, so its name in older AEDC extracts is not E4.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4
value_definition: A two-digit integer with three codes: 0 for no, 1 for yes, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It records attendance ever, not how often or for how long, so a single visit and three years of weekly sessions are the same value. It also does not identify the type of playgroup, so supported and intensive playgroups aimed at families with additional needs cannot be separated from ordinary community ones.
rationale: The dictionary publishes E4 with the playgroup instrument text, the 0/1/88 code list, the 2012 introduction and the 2015 rename from E3b, matching the registry's own description of the column.
evidence_quote: To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended playgroup in the years before entering full time school
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question wording alone with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no warning that the same concept appears as E3b in pre-2015 documentation.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5
variable_description: The teacher's rating of how well the child is settling into school, asked as whether the child "is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school". It is one of three closing instrument questions, with E6 on parental engagement and E7 on reading at home, all sharing the same three-point scale. None of the three feed the five AEDC domain scores, so this column is an independent read on school transition rather than a component of the developmental measures.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is one teacher's global impression at a single point in the child's first school year, not a validated scale, so it cannot be treated as an outcome measure comparable to a domain score. The three points are ordinal and unequally spaced, so averaging them across a school or community produces a number with no defined unit.
rationale: The dictionary gives E5's instrument text, its purpose and its four-code value list, and section 3.1 sets out separately which items build the domain scores.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Child is adapting to school' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the three-point rating scale and the 88 don't-know code were undocumented.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6
variable_description: The teacher's rating of whether the child's parents or caregivers are actively engaged with the school in supporting the child's learning. It is the school-side view of family involvement, and it pairs with E7, which asks about reading at home, to give two crude proxies for the home learning environment. The dictionary records that it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, a filter that was only lifted in 2015.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: New South Wales children are missing for the first two cycles, so a national trend that ignores this treats a coverage change as a real change in parental engagement. The rating also measures engagement visible to the school, so families who support learning at home without contacting the school score low on something they are doing.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the four-code list, and an explicit note that the item was not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 with the filter revised in 2015.
evidence_quote: Not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1/2
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Parents actively engaged with the school' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and omitted the New South Wales coverage gap that makes early-cycle national estimates wrong.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7
variable_description: The teacher's rating of whether the child is regularly read to, or encouraged in reading, at home. The question wording ends "as far as you can tell", which flags on the instrument itself that the teacher is inferring a home behaviour rather than observing it. Like E6, it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, and the same three-point scale is used for both.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is a teacher's inference about the household, so it will partly track how much contact the family has with the school rather than what happens at home. value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Which of four percentile bands the child's emotional maturity score falls into, where band 1 is the AEDC definition of developmentally vulnerable on this domain. The bands are 0 to 10th, 11th to 25th, 26th to 50th and 51st to 100th percentile, so band 1 is vulnerable, band 2 is at risk and bands 3 and 4 are on track. The cut-offs are fixed against the 2009 national collection: the dictionary states they "have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared".
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th. The percentile positions are those of the 2009 baseline distribution, adjusted for age variation across children in their first year of school.
limitation: The bands do not describe the current cohort, so a 12 per cent vulnerable rate in 2021 means 12 per cent scored below the 2009 tenth percentile, not that 12 per cent were in the bottom decile of 2021. The dictionary also states that domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs or aged under four, so their category is absent rather than high.
rationale: The dictionary gives EMOTCategory's four-band value list and section 3.1 explains that the cut-offs are anchored to the 2009 baseline and are not calculated for special needs children or children under four.
evidence_quote: The cut-off scores used in 2009 have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Vulnerable - emotional maturity' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which implied a yes/no flag when the column is in fact a four-band percentile grouping anchored to 2009.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child's emotional maturity result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. The dictionary defines a 1 as "Child does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain", so a single flag folds three separate exclusions together. There is one of these per domain, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of the five a child is valid on.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for this domain; 1 otherwise.
limitation: A 0 does not tell you which of the three reasons applied, so it cannot be used to identify children with special needs or to measure teacher non-response. It is also domain specific, so a child can be valid on physical health and invalid on emotional maturity, and dropping every row with any invalid flag discards usable results on the other domains.
rationale: The dictionary gives the exact two-value list for EMOTValid, naming the three exclusion reasons that collapse into the 0 code, and documents the parallel per-domain flags and the VALIDDOMAINS counter.
evidence_quote: Child has special needs status, is 3 years old or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Valid - emotional maturity' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that special needs status and age three are folded into the same 0 as item non-response.

variable_description: Whether the teacher considers the child to have English as a second language, asked on the instrument as "Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)". It is one of three overlapping language columns and the most subjective: LANG asks whether a language other than English is spoken at home, and LBOTE is derived rather than asked. rationale: The dictionary publishes ESL as an instrument item with its exact question wording and a 0/1 value list, and documents Lang, LBOTE and B1 as the separate language variables it is often confused with.

variable_description: Whether the child speaks a language other than English at home, asked on the instrument as "Does the child speak a language other than English at home". value_domain: AEDC domain score, zero to ten
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: The child's score on the language and cognitive skills domain, which the AEDC qualifies as school-based because the items ask what the teacher observes the child doing in the classroom. LANGCOG_1 to LANGCOG_4 on the same row split it into basic literacy, interest in literacy and numeracy and memory, advanced literacy, and basic numeracy. Like the other four domains it runs from zero to ten with higher scores meaning stronger development, and LANGCOGCATEGORY turns it into the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A continuous numeric value from 0 to 10, stored with four decimal places, formed from the domain's instrument items where at least 75 per cent of them were completed.
limitation: It is measured through classroom English, so a child with strong literacy and numeracy in another language can score low on skills they hold; the domain is not a test administered to the child. The derivation is also closed, since the dictionary states the domain score methodologies are licensed intellectual property and not available to the public, so the score cannot be recomputed or audited from the item columns.
rationale: The dictionary defines LANGCOG as the derived school-based language and cognitive skills domain score with a 7.4 numeric format, and section 3.1 gives the zero to ten range, the completion rule and the licensing restriction.
evidence_quote: To identify the child's (school-based) language and cognitive skills domain score.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Language and cognitive skills' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so neither the range, the four sub-domains, nor the school-based qualification was recorded.
