value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Which of four percentile bands the child's language and cognitive skills score falls into, with band 1 marking developmental vulnerability on this domain. Band 2 is the at risk group, and bands 3 and 4 are both on track, which is why the published on track figure combines them. The dictionary notes that the cut-offs "take into account the age variations in the population of children in their first year of schooling", so the bands are age adjusted rather than raw score thresholds.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th, all positioned against the 2009 national baseline.
limitation: Because the boundaries are age adjusted and anchored to 2009, two children with the same LANGCOG score can sit in different bands, so the category cannot be reconstructed by ranking the score column. Children with a special needs diagnosis and children aged three receive no category, so their rows are blank rather than in band 4.
rationale: The dictionary prints the four-band value list for LANGCOGCategory and section 3.1 states that the cut-offs are age adjusted, fixed to the 2009 baseline, and not applied to special needs children or children under four.
evidence_quote: Domain cut-offs take into account the age variations in the population of children in their first year of schooling.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Vulnerable - language and cognition' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which read as a binary flag and hid both the four bands and the age adjustment.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child's language and cognitive skills result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. A 0 means the child has special needs status, is three years old, or left too many of this domain's instrument questions unanswered; a 1 means none of those applied. It is the language and cognition member of a set of five, one per domain, and VALIDINSTRUMENT separately identifies children with fewer than four valid domain scores for the 80 per cent coverage rule.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the domain result is not valid, 1 where it is. The item threshold behind it is the 75 per cent domain completion rule.
limitation: It is a reporting eligibility flag, not a data quality score, so a 1 does not mean every question was answered and a 0 does not mean the teacher failed to respond. Because the same 0 covers special needs status, it is not safe to use this column as a proxy for teacher non-response on the language items.
rationale: The dictionary gives LANGCOGValid's exact two-value list naming the three exclusion reasons, and documents ValidInstrument and ValidDomains as the separate coverage variables.
evidence_quote: To identify the validity of the child's results on the language and cognitive skills (school-based) domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Valid - language and cognitive skills' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never named the three conditions that produce a 0.

variable_description: Whether the teacher relied on a written record, meaning an enrolment form, an assessment or a report, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the documentary option in a six-way multiple response set, LANGSOURCE0 to LANGSOURCE5, that records where the teacher's answer came from. The whole set is answered only where LANG records a language other than English at home.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. Only 2 means the source was used.

rationale: The dictionary gives LangSource0's instrument text naming enrolment form, assessment and report, its purpose of recording the sources behind CanCom, the 'Only answer if Lang = Yes' filter, and the unusual 0/1/2 value list.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the bare option label 'Enrolment form, assessment, report or school survey' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which question the source belongs to or that 1 means no rather than yes.

It is the family-report option in the LANGSOURCE set, and the one that carries most weight for a child whose language the school has no records on. Selecting it does not exclude the other five options, since the underlying instrument question is select all that apply.

value_domain: AEDC language background other than English indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the child has a language background other than English, derived by the AEDC rather than asked of the teacher. It is the third and broadest of the AEDC language flags, and the dictionary prints the rule that builds it: "Children are considered 'LBOTE' if they speak a language other than English at home, or if they speak English at home but are still considered to have ESL (English as a second language) status." It is therefore the union of LANG and ESL, which is why it is always at least as large as either one on its own. The dictionary lists it among the variables whose names, descriptions or notes were corrected in the 2024 revision, so its published definition is not identical across dictionary versions.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes, with the source given as derived rather than instrument. It equals 1 where LANG is 1 or ESL is 1.
limitation: Because it is the union of two flags it cannot be read as either one: an LBOTE rate counts children who speak only English at home but are classed ESL by the teacher, so it inherits the subjectivity of the ESL judgement. Language background is also not proficiency, so an LBOTE rate is not a measure of how many children need English language support.
rationale: The dictionary gives LBOTE as a derived 0/1 indicator distinct from the instrument-collected Lang and ESL items, and names it in the version 7.0 list of variables whose descriptions were corrected.
evidence_quote: To indicate if the child has a Language Background Other Than English (LBOTE).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the acronym as 'LBOTE indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither expanded the abbreviation nor recorded that the column is derived rather than reported.

value_domain: ABS SEIFA Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage score
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 4.2 SEIFA and section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The ABS socio-economic index score for the AEDC Local Community the child lives in, used as the standard area measure of disadvantage in AEDC analysis. The dictionary is explicit about which index: "In AEDC, we use the Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (IRSD)". The Census vintage behind the score changes by cycle, being 2006 for the 2009 collection, 2011 for 2012 and 2015, 2016 for 2018 and 2021 for the 2021 and 2024 collections. LCABSSEIFACATEGORY beside it groups the same score into ordinal bands.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 4.2 SEIFA and section 12 Local Community Based Geography
value_definition: A numeric value stored with four decimal places, on the ABS IRSD scale that is standardised to a national mean near 1000. Where a local community spans more than one SEIFA area, the score is a population-weighted average of the component scores.
limitation: It describes an area, not a family, so using it as a child-level measure of household disadvantage is an ecological inference and will understate the spread within a community. The IRSD also measures disadvantage only, and the ABS warns it is not a measure of advantage, so a high score means an absence of disadvantage rather than affluence; and because the Census vintage changes between cycles, part of any movement in the score is a change of index rather than a change of the place.
rationale: The dictionary names the specific SEIFA index the AEDC uses, prints the cycle-by-cycle table of SEIFA vintages for local community scores, and explains the population-weighted recalculation used where boundaries split.
evidence_quote: In AEDC, we use the Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (IRSD).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local community seifa score' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say which of the four SEIFA indexes was used, nor that the vintage differs by collection cycle.

variable_description: A count, from zero to five, of the developmental domains on which the child scored in the bottom tenth of the 2009 national distribution. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify the number of domains in which the child is in the 0 to 10th percentile category", so it is the number of the five category columns - PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY - that equal 1. HIGHTOTAL is its mirror at the other end of the distribution, and the published summary indicators DV1 and DV2 are yes/no readings of this same count.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'LowTotal'

A domain that could not be scored is simply not counted, which means a low value can mean strong development or missing information; VALIDDOMAINS and TOTALMISS are what tell those apart.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary publishes LowTotal as a derived variable with an explicit purpose statement naming the percentile band, and the surrounding category and validity columns in the PLIDA core tables show exactly what it is summing.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on one or more of the five domains, calculated on the same basis as the vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2. The dictionary defines it as "On Track - On one or more domain" and records it as introduced for the 2024 collection, when the legacy ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 columns were recalculated; PLIDA carries it from the 2018 cycle, so the rebuilt series has been applied back across the earlier files. A rate from this column has to be taken over children with OT1FLAG equal to 1.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1' and section 6
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. It is derived from the five domain category columns; the summary indicators carry no score and no cut-off of their own.
limitation: One or more domains on track is a very low bar and is not the AEDC's headline strengths measure, which is OT5 across all five. Reading a high rate here as good news inverts the intent, because the indicator is passed by a child who is developmentally vulnerable on the other four domains.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element, its purpose, its permitted values and the 2024 change note that created it out of the legacy ONTRACK1 column, and section 3.2 explains why the summary indicators have no score.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on one or more domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not mention OT1FLAG, without which the column produces a number that is not the published rate.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child counts in the denominator when an on-track-on-one-or-more rate is worked out. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT1" and its purpose as identifying whether the child qualifies for that calculation; AEDC summary indicators are published as percentages of qualifying children, not of every row on the file. It is the strengths-side equivalent of DV1FLAG, and filtering on it before averaging OT1 is the difference between the published rate and a number that merely resembles it.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1Flag'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It does not say why a child was excluded. The AEDC's exclusion rules cover children with diagnosed special needs, children aged three and children with too many unanswered instrument items, and all three land on the same zero, so SPECIALNEEDS, the age columns and the five domain validity columns are needed to tell them apart.
rationale: The dictionary publishes a separate flag element for each on-track threshold with its own purpose statement, and the domain validity entries give the exclusion rules the flags implement.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally on track on one or more domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long phrase with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never explained what a denominator flag is for or what a zero can mean.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2'
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as "On Track - On two or more domains". It is one of the four sub-threshold companions to OT5, created in 2024 so the whole on-track ladder is calculated the way the national indicators are, and it is reported over the OT2FLAG denominator rather than over all rows. The 2009 to 2015 files hold the older ONTRACK2 in its place.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from how many of the five domain category columns place the child above the 25th percentile.
limitation: The AEDC publishes no two-or-more on-track rate, so a figure from this column cannot be checked against a national report. It is also not the mirror of DV2: DV2 counts vulnerability on two or more domains, and a child can be flagged on both columns at once.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its purpose and its values, and section 3.2 lists the three indicators the AEDC actually reports, which does not include this threshold.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on two or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line with the duplicated generic sentence, so it neither named the denominator flag nor warned that the column has no published counterpart.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-two-or-more rate. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT2", introduced in 2024 alongside OT2 itself when the legacy ONTRACK series was rebuilt with explicit denominators. Each on-track threshold has its own flag, so this one qualifies a child for OT2 and for nothing else.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2Flag'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: A denominator flag is not a data-quality flag for the whole row. A child excluded here can still have usable domain scores, geography and demographics, so dropping records on this flag discards analysis that has nothing to do with the summary indicator.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the flag as its own data element with a purpose limited to the OT2 calculation, which establishes both its role and its narrow scope.
evidence_quote: Qualifies for the denominator of OT2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not distinguish a denominator rule from a record-level quality flag.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3'
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as "On Track - On three or more domains". It sits in the middle of the OT1 to OT5 ladder introduced for the 2024 collection, and like the rest of that ladder it is meant to be averaged only over children whose matching flag, OT3FLAG, equals 1. Its 2009 to 2015 predecessor is ONTRACK3.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. The thresholds are cumulative, so a child flagged on OT4 or OT5 is also flagged here.
limitation: Subtracting the OT4 rate from the OT3 rate does not give the share on track on exactly three domains, because OT3FLAG and OT4FLAG are separate columns that need not qualify the same children. Nor does the count carry a developmental meaning - each domain has its own cut-off, so moving from three to four is not a fixed increment of development.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element and a separate denominator flag entry for each threshold, which is what establishes that thresholds cannot be differenced without checking the flags.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on three or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording with the generic sentence printed twice, so it gave no hint that each threshold carries its own denominator rule.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-three-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT3". It was introduced for the 2024 collection with OT3, part of giving every on-track threshold the kind of explicit denominator the vulnerability indicators had carried since 2009. Without it, an average of OT3 runs over children the AEDC does not count.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3Flag'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It qualifies the child for one threshold only, so a denominator built once from this column and reused across OT1 to OT5 will not reproduce the published rates. The dictionary does not publish the qualification rule behind it either, so the flag has to be read from the file rather than rebuilt from the five domain validity columns.
rationale: The dictionary gives each threshold its own flag element with its own purpose, which is the evidence that the flags are not interchangeable.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally on track on three or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, so a reader could reasonably have assumed one flag serves all the on-track columns.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4'
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as "On Track - On four or more domains". It is the closest threshold below OT5, the AEDC's national strengths indicator, and it was created in 2024 when the legacy ONTRACK columns were recalculated onto the OT5 method. Rates need the OT4FLAG denominator.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns rather than from a score.
limitation: It is not the opposite of DV1: a child on track on four domains and developmentally vulnerable on the fifth reads 1 on both columns, so the pair cannot be treated as two ends of one scale. It also does not identify which domain the child fell short on, which only the five category columns show.
rationale: The dictionary carries the element and its purpose, and section 3.2 describes the vulnerability and strengths indicators as separate measures rather than complements.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on four or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, leaving the reader to assume wrongly that a child on track on four domains cannot be counted as developmentally vulnerable.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-four-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT4". It is one of the four flags added in 2024 when OT1 to OT4 were created, modelled on DV1FLAG and DV2FLAG so that every AEDC indicator states who it is calculated over. It applies to OT4 only.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4Flag'
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It is not interchangeable with DV1FLAG or DV2FLAG. The strengths and vulnerability denominators were aligned in method rather than merged, so each indicator keeps its own flag and a single 'valid children' total cannot serve both families of indicators.
rationale: Appendix 3 explains that the strengths indicator was recalculated to align with the vulnerability indicators, and the dictionary still lists a separate flag element for each, which shows alignment did not mean a shared denominator column.
evidence_quote: Qualifies for the denominator of OT4.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's phrase with the generic sentence twice and gave no warning against reusing the vulnerability denominators for the strengths indicators.

value_domain: AEDC On Track on Five national summary indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5' and section 3.2
variable_description: The AEDC's national strengths measure: a yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on every one of the five domains. The dictionary calls it the third summary indicator and describes it as "a strength-based indicator" beside the two vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2, and it was created in 2021 so that the strengths measure would be calculated the same way they are. It is the variable behind the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap tracking, and rates must be taken over children with OT5FLAG equal to 1.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5' and section 3.2
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. Like the vulnerability indicators it has no score and no cut-off of its own, resting on whether the child is on track on each domain separately.
limitation: It is not the opposite of DV1. A child who is at risk rather than vulnerable on one domain reads 0 here and 0 on DV1, so the two indicators leave a middle group neither counts and one minus the OT5 rate is not the vulnerability rate. Results from 2018 onward also cannot be joined to ONTRACK5 in the 2009 to 2015 files, which uses the superseded calculation.
rationale: The dictionary defines the element, section 3.2 sets out its status as one of three national summary indicators and explains that summary indicators carry no score, and Appendix 3 records why it replaced ONTRACK5.
evidence_quote: The third summary indicator, On Track on Five domains (OT5) is a strength-based indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Child is developmentally on track on all five domains' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and so omitted the denominator flag, the 2021 recalculation and the break with ONTRACK5.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5Flag' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
variable_description: Marks whether the child counts in the denominator of the on-track-on-all-five rate, the AEDC's national strengths indicator. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT5" and records it as created in 2021 with OT5 itself, so that the strengths measure would carry the same kind of qualification rule as DV1FLAG and DV2FLAG. It is the flag the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap tracking rests on, so an OT5 rate calculated without it will not match the published series.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5Flag' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It is not a general statement that the child has five usable domain scores; that is what VALIDDOMAINS counts. Applying it to a different indicator, or applying it after averaging rather than before, changes the number away from the published one.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the flag element and Appendix 3 explains that refining the denominator was the whole reason the OT5 pair was created, which is what makes the flag load-bearing rather than incidental.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally on track on all five domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the national strengths figure is defined by this flag.

value_domain: Gender of first listed parent or carer (school enrolment)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Gender'
variable_description: The recorded gender of the adult listed first on the child's school enrolment, pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument. It identifies whichever adult the school listed first, which need not be a mother, a birth parent or an adult living with the child. With PARENT2GENDER it is the only signal in the AEDC core file about the adults around the child, and it appears from the 2018 cycle onward.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Gender'
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Male, 2 Female, 9 Not stated. There is no non-binary category and no code separating a refusal from an unrecorded value.
limitation: It cannot identify family structure. A missing PARENT2GENDER can mean one adult on the enrolment form, a school that recorded only one contact, or a second adult whose details were withheld, and none of those is the same as a single-parent household.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its three permitted values and, crucially, that the source is pre-population from school enrolment rather than the AEDC instrument, which is what limits how the column can be read.
evidence_quote: Gender of first parent or carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'First parent or carer gender' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say the value comes from the enrolment record or that 'parent 1' is only an ordering on a form.

value_domain: School enrolment parental occupation group (four bands)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Occup'
variable_description: The occupation group of the first adult on the child's enrolment, in the four broad bands Australian schools collect at enrolment. The dictionary runs them from group 1, "Senior management in large business organisation, government administration and defence, and qualified professionals", down to group 4, "Machine operators, hospitality staff, assistants, labourers and related workers", with 8 for not in paid work in the last 12 months and 9 for not stated. It is pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument, and it exists only from the 2021 cycle.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Occup'
value_definition: A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 or 9. It is a broad skill-level grouping rather than an ANZSCO code, so it cannot be resolved to an occupation title or an industry.
limitation: Code 8 is not unemployment: it covers anyone not in paid work in the previous twelve months, including carers, students and retirees, and it sits outside the 1-to-4 order rather than below group 4. Because the value is copied from the enrolment form, it also describes the adult's work when the child enrolled, which can be a year or more before the assessment.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with the full label for each group and records the source as pre-population, which establishes both the classification and why the value is not contemporaneous with the assessment.
evidence_quote: Senior management in large business organisation, government administration and defence, and qualified professionals
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Occupation group of first parent or carer' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say the groups are broad skill bands or that code 8 is not part of the ordering.

value_domain: Highest post-school qualification, first parent or carer
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1PostSchool'
variable_description: The highest post-school qualification held by the first adult on the child's enrolment, in four broad bands from a bachelor degree down to none. The dictionary gives the collection wording as "What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1" and records the column as available in both the Complete and Core files, while PARENT1SCHOOL is listed for the Complete file only. PARENT2POSTSCHOOL holds the same measure for the second adult.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1PostSchool'
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Bachelor degree or above, 2 Advanced Diploma or Diploma, 3 Certificate level I to IV including trade qualification, 4 No post-school qualification, 88 Not known.
limitation: Code 4 is a substantive answer and 88 is the missing one, so pooling them turns parents whose qualification was not recorded into parents with none. The bands also run a Certificate I and a Certificate IV together, which covers a wide range of labour-market positions inside a single code.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with its instrument wording, its availability across file types and the full code list including the distinct 'no qualification' and 'not known' values.
evidence_quote: What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Post-school qualification of first parent or carer' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate code 4 from code 88, which is the mistake this column invites.

value_domain: Highest school year completed, first parent or carer
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1School'
variable_description: The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the adult listed first on the child's enrolment, banded into four levels. The dictionary gives the collection wording as "What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1", so the answer comes from the enrolment form rather than from the teacher. PARENT1POSTSCHOOL holds the same adult's post-school qualification, and the two must be read together because a parent with a degree still records a school year here.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1School'
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Year 12 or equivalent, 2 Year 11, 3 Year 10, 4 Year 9 or equivalent or below, 88 Not known.
limitation: The scale runs backwards, so a higher code means less schooling and any model that treats the raw code as an education score inverts the result. 'Parent or carer 1' is also only the first adult on the enrolment form, so this is not the mother's education, the resident parent's education or the higher of the two.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with its instrument wording and the full four-band code list plus the 88 missing code, which is exactly what a user needs to avoid inverting the scale.
evidence_quote: What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'School level completed by first parent or carer' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding both the reversed coding and the 88 missing convention.

value_domain: Gender of second listed parent or carer (school enrolment)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Gender'
variable_description: The recorded gender of the second adult on the child's school enrolment, present only where the school listed a second parent or carer. Like the first-parent column it is pre-populated from enrolment rather than collected by the AEDC, so it follows whatever the school held rather than the child's living arrangements when the instrument was completed. Paired with PARENT1GENDER it is sometimes used to approximate two-parent or same-sex households, which the AEDC does not itself measure.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Gender'
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Male, 2 Female, 9 Not stated. The value is absent rather than zero where no second adult was recorded.
limitation: This is the weakest basis in the file for inferring household type: a 9 and an absent second parent look similar in analysis but mean different things, and neither confirms who lived with the child. The AEDC records no relationship, so 'parent or carer 2' can be a grandparent, a step-parent or another guardian.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with the same three values as the first-parent column and records its source as pre-population, which establishes both the coding and the reason a gap is ambiguous.
evidence_quote: Gender of second parent or carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Second parent or carer gender' with the duplicated generic sentence, and so invited the common mistake of reading a blank as a single-parent household.

value_domain: School enrolment parental occupation group (four bands)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Occup'
variable_description: The occupation group of the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify the occupation of the second parent or carer" and records the source as pre-population from the enrolment record, so it is not something the teacher supplied. variable_description: Which band of the 2009 national distribution the child's physical health and wellbeing score falls into: 1 is "0 to 10th percentile", 2 is "11th to 25th percentile", 3 is the 26th to 50th and 4 the 51st to 100th. limitation: It is not a quartile of the current cohort, so a rising share in band 4 means children doing better than 2009 children rather than better than their peers. The bands are also unequal in width - 10, 15, 25 and 50 percentage points - so treating the codes as an evenly spaced scale misreads the distribution.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the four percentile bands verbatim and section 3.1 states that the cut-offs come from the 2009 baseline and are held constant across cycles.

It is the filter to apply before analysing PHYS or PHYSCATEGORY, and each of the five domains has its own version, so a child can be valid on one domain and not another.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD quintile, national, at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFACategory
variable_description: The national disadvantage quintile of the small area the child lives in, which the dictionary states as "SEIFA – IRSD category (quintile) within Australia". The underlying measure is the ABS Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage computed from Census data for the child's Statistical Area Level 1, so it describes the neighbourhood and not the household. It is the socio-economic field carried in every AEDC cycle table here, where SEIFADECILE and SEIFAPERCENTILE appear only from the 2018 file onward, and it is distinct from LCABSSEIFACATEGORY, which reports SEIFA for the much larger AEDC local community, built by population-weighted averaging of the component area scores.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFACategory
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 1 to 5, where 1 is quintile 1 (most disadvantaged) and 5 is quintile 5 (least disadvantaged); the dictionary declares the field as an eight-length integer.
limitation: A quintile of an area is not a measure of a family, and many children in the most advantaged quintile live in poor households, so reading category 1 as 'this child is disadvantaged' is the ecological fallacy the ABS warns against. The quintiles are also cut nationally, so a state where few areas fall in quintile 1 has fewer children in that category by geography rather than by need, and the cut points move between SEIFA releases rather than between cycles: the dictionary records the 2011 SEIFA behind the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles, the 2016 SEIFA behind 2018, and the 2021 SEIFA behind both 2021 and 2024.
rationale: The dictionary's SEIFACategory entry gives the purpose statement naming IRSD quintiles within Australia and prints all five labelled values, and the ABS SEIFA release defines IRSD itself.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD category (quintile) within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'SEIFA category' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it named neither the index, nor the direction of the scale, nor the geography it is measured on.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD decile, national, at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFADecile
variable_description: The national disadvantage decile of the small area the child lives in, given by the dictionary as "SEIFA – IRSD decile within Australia", and a finer cut of the ranking SEIFACATEGORY holds in quintiles. The ABS builds it by ordering every Statistical Area Level 1 by its IRSD score and splitting the ordered list into ten equal groups, so the value is a position in the national distribution rather than a quantity. In this registry it appears only in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables, alongside SEIFAPERCENTILE and SEIFARANK, which is why an analysis spanning all six cycles has to fall back on SEIFACATEGORY.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFADecile
value_definition: A two-digit integer from 1 to 10. The ABS assigns it by rank: "All areas are ordered from lowest to highest score, the lowest 10% of areas are given a decile number of one...up to the highest 10% of areas which are given a decile number of 10", so 1 is the most disadvantaged tenth.
limitation: Deciles are ranks, so the gap between decile 1 and decile 2 is not the same amount of disadvantage as the gap between decile 5 and decile 6, and averaging them produces a number with no interpretation. The decile also comes from the SEIFA release the dictionary assigns to the cycle, the 2016 SEIFA for 2018 and the 2021 SEIFA for both 2021 and 2024, so an area that keeps the same decile across cycles has kept its position relative to other areas rather than its circumstances.
rationale: The dictionary defines the field as the national IRSD decile and gives its two-digit integer format, and the ABS SEIFA technical paper defines how deciles are formed from ranked SA1 scores.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD decile within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Seifa - irsd decile within australia' as its whole description with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said that the values run 1 to 10 with 1 most disadvantaged, nor that the column is missing from half the AEDC cycles in this asset.

variable_description: A marker that the child's small area has no SEIFA score to report, which the dictionary describes as denoting "SEIFA – Denotes unavailability of SEIFA data in particular statistical areas". It exists because the ABS does not score every Statistical Area Level 1: published exclusion rules drop areas with no or very small populations, with very few employed people or classifiable private dwellings, and with most people counted in non-private dwellings, and those areas are left without an index value. Read it before using SEIFASCORE, SEIFACATEGORY, SEIFADECILE or SEIFAPERCENTILE, since it is the column that tells you an empty or implausible value there is a deliberate absence rather than a data fault.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD index score at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAScore
variable_description: The underlying disadvantage index value for the child's neighbourhood, which the dictionary defines as the "SEIFA – IRSD score based on the SA1 in which the child lives". The ABS builds the Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage from Census variables such as low income, low educational attainment, unemployment and crowded dwellings, then rescales the result, so a lower score means more disadvantage. In this asset the column is present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables only; the later cycles carry the ranked forms in SEIFARANK, SEIFADECILE and SEIFAPERCENTILE instead.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAScore
value_definition: A numeric field declared as 12.8, so up to eight decimal places. The ABS standardises index scores across all scored areas: "We then rescale the raw scores to a mean of 1,000 and standard deviation of 100 to create a new set of scores that are the index scores in SEIFA."
limitation: The scale is set within each SEIFA release, so a score of 950 in the 2011-based index and 950 in the 2016-based index describe a similar position among areas of their day, not the same living conditions. The three cycles that carry this column all draw on the 2011 SEIFA, so a difference in score between them reflects a different area rather than a change in an area's circumstances. The index also summarises disadvantage only, so a high score is an absence of measured disadvantage rather than evidence of advantage, which is a separate ABS index.
rationale: The dictionary's SEIFAScore entry names the index, the geography and the numeric format, and the ABS SEIFA technical paper gives the standardisation that fixes what the number means.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD score based on the SA1 in which the child lives.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCCategory
variable_description: Where the child's social competence score sits against the fixed 2009 national cut-offs, banded into four percentile ranges. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify the grouping variable for the cumulative frequency of scores in the social competence domain", and it is the column that produces published AEDC reporting: band 1 is developmentally vulnerable on this domain, band 2 is developmentally at risk, and bands 3 and 4 are on track. It also feeds the summary indicators, since DV1 and DV2 count how many of the five domain categories fall in band 1.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCCategory
value_definition: A single-digit integer with four values: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th. The percentiles are the cut-off scores set in the 2009 collection and held constant since.
limitation: The bands are not recomputed each cycle, so they do not divide the current cohort into fixed shares: finding more or fewer than 10 per cent of children in band 1 in 2021 is the result rather than an error. The column is also not calculated for every child, since categories are only produced where the domain score is valid, which excludes children with special needs status and children aged three.
rationale: The dictionary's SOCCategory entry publishes the four percentile bands in full, and its section 3.1 records that the cut-offs come from the 2009 baseline and have been held constant to keep later cycles comparable.
evidence_quote: To identify the grouping variable for the cumulative frequency of scores in the social competence domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Vulnerable - social competence' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, implying a yes-or-no vulnerability flag when the column actually holds a four-band percentile grouping in which only band 1 means vulnerable.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCValid
variable_description: Whether this child's social competence result may be used, which the dictionary states as being "To identify the validity of the child's results on the social competence domain". It is the gate on SOC and SOCCATEGORY: a child can carry a stored score while this column says the score does not qualify for reporting. Each of the five domains has its own flag of this shape, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of them are set to 1 for the child.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCValid
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 where the child "does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain", and 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain.
limitation: A 0 does not tell you which of its three causes applied, so it cannot be used as a measure of item non-response; SPECIALNEEDS and the age fields have to be checked to separate a child excluded by rule from one whose teacher left questions blank. It is also a statement about this domain only, not about the instrument as a whole, which is what VALIDINSTRUMENT covers.
rationale: The dictionary's SOCValid entry gives the purpose statement and both labelled values, including the three conditions that force a zero.
evidence_quote: To identify the validity of the child's results on the social competence domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Valid - social competence' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never revealed that invalidity mixes an administrative exclusion with genuine missing responses.

value_source: AEDC Data Guidelines (Australian Government Department of Education, 2025), glossary entry Special needs, with the code frame in the AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 entry SpecialNeeds
variable_description: Whether the teacher recorded the child as having special needs status when completing the instrument. The Data Guidelines define the term as applying to "children reported by teachers as requiring special assistance because of chronic medical, physical, or intellectually disabling conditions (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome) based on a medical diagnosis or diagnoses". The value governs most of the rest of the record: children flagged 1 are counted in the AEDC population, but their domain results are ruled invalid and their domain categories are not calculated, which is why the published denominators, and the 80 per cent coverage rule that VALIDINSTRUMENT serves, count only children with SPECIALNEEDS = 0.
description_source: AEDC Data Guidelines (Australian Government Department of Education, 2025), glossary entry Special needs, with the code frame in the AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 entry SpecialNeeds
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 0 for not special needs and 1 for special needs. The item is asked of the teacher as "Is this child considered Special Needs".
limitation: It is the teacher's report at the time of the collection, made against a medical diagnosis but recorded through school processes, so the share flagged is not a prevalence estimate for disability and should not be compared between jurisdictions without care. It also says nothing about the condition itself, which the D-series items on the AEDC special needs table carry.
rationale: The AEDC Data Guidelines glossary defines special needs status and sets out its role in the coverage rule denominator, and the Data Dictionary publishes the two-value code frame and the instrument wording.
evidence_quote: Term applying to children reported by teachers as requiring special assistance because of chronic medical, physical, or intellectually disabling conditions (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome) based on a medical diagnosis or diagnoses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's 'Special needs status' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, hiding the fact that this one flag suppresses every domain score and category on the row.

value_domain: AEDC state electoral division publication reason code
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateElectoratePublic
variable_description: Whether AEDC results may be published for the state electoral division the child lives in, and if not, which rule stopped them. The dictionary describes the field as the "SED reportability indicator" and prints six codes, one meaning publishable and five naming a specific failure: too few valid children, too few teachers, both, coverage below 80 per cent of non-special-needs children, or no location. It is the electorate member of a family of publication codes that also covers communities (CPUBLIC), local communities (LCPUBLIC), Indigenous areas (IAREPUBLIC) and statistical areas, and it appears in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables only.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateElectoratePublic

limitation: It is a rule about reporting an area, not a judgement on the child: a code of 21 or 22 does not mean this row is unreliable, only that the electorate it belongs to is too thin to report. It also carries nothing about which electoral boundaries applied, so it cannot be used to align a cycle's results with a particular redistribution; STATEELECTORATECODE and STATEELECTORATE hold the identity of the division.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation
variable_description: The person key that ties a child's AEDC record to the rest of PLIDA, and the reason the collection is in this asset at all. Within AEDC it joins the five tables of a cycle, so a child's core record, domain scores, instrument background, language detail and special needs detail assemble on this column; across the asset it is the same key the Census, births, MBS, PBS, DOMINO and the tax products carry, so an AvEDI result can be read against a child's birth record, health history or family's payment history. ABS lists the AEDC among PLIDA's linked sources, naming the 2009, 2012, 2015 and 2018 collections on its data page while this asset carries six cycles, and the linkage is performed centrally against the person linkage spine rather than by matching names in this file.
description_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned for linkage with no meaning in its digits. It is not a student number, an enrolment identifier or an AEDC instrument identifier, so it can be matched but not decoded.
limitation: A child appears here only where their AvEDI record linked to the spine, and children who did not link are missing rather than untested, so AEDC coverage in PLIDA is lower than AEDC coverage in the national collection and the shortfall should not be assumed random. The key is also for the child, not the class or the family: TEACHERID and SCHOOLID group the record, and no parent or sibling identifier is carried, so a family cannot be assembled from this column alone.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA data page lists the Australian Early Development Census among the datasets brought into the asset and describes the central linkage of person records, which is what this column carries; the custodian description in the PLIDA data item list names it as the synthetic person identifier used across products.
evidence_quote: Australian Early Development Census, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018 - Measures how well children in their first year of full time school are developing across 5 important domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 30 occurrences it never said that this is the column joining the five AEDC tables to each other and the AEDC to the rest of PLIDA, nor that linkage failure, not absence of assessment, explains a missing child.

value_domain: Teacher Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status (three values)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI
variable_description: Whether the teacher who completed the instrument identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, asked directly as "Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent". It sits in the instrument background table with the CONSULTTYPE items about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural consultants, and the point of the block is to describe who did the assessing rather than who was assessed. It is the column to use when testing whether teacher background is associated with reported outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, whose own status is on ATSI in the core table.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three values: 0 the teacher was not Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, 1 the teacher was, and 2 the teacher responded inconsistently to their own Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status.
limitation: It describes the teacher, not the child, so it cannot stand in for the child's Indigenous status anywhere. Code 2 is also a data quality state rather than a third identity: it marks contradictory answers within the teacher's own record, so quietly dropping it or folding it into 0 shifts the measured share of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander teachers in an unknown direction.
rationale: The dictionary's TeacherATSI entry gives the origin definition, the instrument wording and all three labelled values, including the inconsistent-response code.
evidence_quote: Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Indigenous teacher' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it read as a yes-or-no flag and hid the third code for inconsistent responses.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID
variable_description: Which teacher filled in the instrument for this child, as a de-identified number. The dictionary describes it as a "unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information", and its analytic value is as the clustering unit: every AvEDI score is one teacher's judgement of one child, so children sharing a value here share a rater and their scores are not independent observations. SCHOOLID nests these teachers within schools, and CLASSTYPEA_1, CLASSTYPEB and CLASSTYPEC describe the class the teacher was reporting on.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID
value_definition: A right-justified integer, allocated for the collection and carrying no information about the teacher. The dictionary's variable page gives it a length of 11, while its appendix metadata shows the narrower format F6.0.
limitation: It is not a person key on the PLIDA spine, so a teacher cannot be joined to their own tax, payment or health records the way a child can through SYNTHETIC_AEUID; nothing about the teacher beyond TEACHERATSI is available. The dictionary also does not state that the code is stable between collections, so it should not be used to follow one teacher from 2009 to a later cycle.
rationale: The dictionary's TeacherID entry defines the code as unique and non-identifying and gives its integer format; the registry shows the field beside SCHOOLID and the class-type items that make it a clustering variable.
evidence_quote: The Teacher ID uses a unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Teacher identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never told a reader that this is the rater key their standard errors should account for, or that it does not reach the PLIDA spine.

value_domain: Time in class under one month, with completion intent (three values)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch
variable_description: Whether the child had been in class for less than one month when the instrument was started, and if so whether the teacher went on to fill it in anyway. The dictionary's reason for asking is that "If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC", and the teacher may then stop. This is why a row can exist with almost nothing on it: a value of 1 here is the explanation for empty domain scores and empty instrument items, and CANASSESS, asked only when this is a yes, records whether the teacher felt able to assess the child at all.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three values: 0 no, 1 yes and skip the rest of the instrument, and 2 yes but the rest of the instrument will be completed.
limitation: The instrument asks about time in this class while the dictionary's description speaks of time at school, so a child who transferred in October after a full year elsewhere may be coded the same as a child who started school that month. It is also not a data quality flag on the responses that follow: a 1 means there are no responses to judge, while a 2 means the teacher went ahead on under a month's acquaintance and the scores stand in the file unmarked.
rationale: The dictionary's Tmsch entry gives the rationale, the instrument wording and all three values, including the distinction between skipping and completing the rest of the instrument, and records CanAssess as the follow-up item.
evidence_quote: If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'In school for less than one month' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it read as a yes-or-no flag and never explained that one of its two yes values means the rest of the row was deliberately left blank.

value_domain: Count of missing domain scales (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss
variable_description: How many of the five AEDC scales could not be calculated for this child, defined by the dictionary as the "Total number of missing scales (0-5)". It is the sum of the five per-scale missing flags PHMiss, SCMiss, EMMiss, LCMiss and CGMiss, which the dictionary restricts to the master unit record file and which are not carried in the AEDC tables in this asset, so this count is the only summary of scale-level missingness available here. A scale goes missing when fewer than 75 per cent of that domain's instrument items were answered.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5, one unit for each of physical health and wellbeing, social competence, emotional maturity, language and cognitive skills, and communication and general knowledge.
limitation: It does not say which scales are missing, so a value of 2 needs the five domain score columns checked one by one before an analysis can decide whether the loss matters. It is also not the complement of VALIDDOMAINS: a scale can be computed and still be ruled invalid because the child has special needs status or is three years old, so the two columns need not add to five.
rationale: The dictionary's TotalMiss entry gives the definition, the purpose and the 0 to 5 integer format, and the five per-scale flags immediately before it in the same section show what is being counted and that they are master-file-only fields.
evidence_quote: Total number of missing scales (0-5).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Total number of missing scales (0-5)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no hint that the per-scale flags behind the count are absent from this asset.

value_domain: Count of valid domain scores (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains
variable_description: How many of the five AEDC domains yielded a usable score for this child, which the dictionary gives as being "To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid". It is the total of the five per-domain flags PHYSVALID, SOCVALID, EMOTVALID, LANGCOGVALID and COMGENVALID, and it is the input to the reporting rule: children with fewer than four valid domains are the ones VALIDINSTRUMENT marks as not counting. Use it as the first filter on any analysis of domain scores, ahead of the individual flags.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5. The dictionary publishes no value labels because the number is simply the count of domains for which the validity conditions were met.
limitation: A 0 does not mean an empty instrument. Children with special needs status have no valid domain scores by rule, so they sit at 0 while their teacher may have answered every question, and reading this column as a response-quality measure conflates an administrative exclusion with missing data. value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidInstrument
variable_description: Whether this child's completed instrument counts as valid for AEDC reporting, set from the number of domains that produced a score. The dictionary states the purpose as "To identify children with less than 4 valid domain scores for the purpose of calculating the 80 per cent Coverage Rule", the rule requiring that 80 per cent of the children in an area hold valid instruments before results for that area may be published. The AEDC Data Guidelines set out the arithmetic: divide the count of records with VALIDINSTRUMENT = 1 by the count with SPECIALNEEDS = 0. The dictionary records that the field was called ValidChecklist before the 2015 collection.
description_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidInstrument
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 0 for no and 1 for yes, derived from VALIDDOMAINS with the threshold at four of the five domains.
limitation: A 0 is not a verdict on the teacher's answers. A child with special needs status has no valid domain scores by rule and therefore fails the four-domain test while holding a fully answered instrument, which is exactly why the coverage rule counts only children with SPECIALNEEDS = 0 in its denominator. rationale: The dictionary's ValidInstrument entry gives the purpose, the two-value code frame and the 2015 rename, and the AEDC Data Guidelines give the 80 per cent coverage rule and the exact numerator and denominator this flag is used in.
evidence_quote: To identify children with less than 4 valid domain scores for the purpose of calculating the 80 per cent Coverage Rule.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address of a business location. A business with several sites has one row per location, so this identifier is what makes a site the unit of analysis rather than the business, and what follows a site across years and across changes of owning entity. It is the same address key the person-level products use, which is why a business location and a residence can be recognised as the same address without either holding one.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated, which the BLADE Data Item List gives as 24 alphanumeric characters. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a business or a site, so businesses sharing a building share the value, and a registered office that is an accountant's address is indistinguishable from a place of work. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The BLADE Data Item List names the field as a deidentified ARID on the Business Locations table and gives its valid response as 24 alphanumeric. ABS publishes what the Address Register and its identifier are.
evidence_quote: Identifier - deidentified ARID
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the DIL wording 'Identifier - deidentified ARID' with no explanation of what an ARID is, and gave its domain as 'open numeric domain' when the stored value is alphanumeric.

value_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
variable_description: The partnership, trust or company the individual held an interest in. Business ownership is recorded as a link between a person and an entity, and this is the entity half of that link, so it is what turns the file from a list of people into a list of ownership relationships. The same entity carries the same value in BLADE and in the ATO products, which is how an owner can be followed to the business they own.
description_source: Australian Business Register, ABN format
value_definition: A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as "a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register", structured as "a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded and is useful only for matching one record to another.
limitation: The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a business as a going concern. A structure with several entities appears as several identifiers with nothing linking them, and an entity that restructures takes a new ABN, so continuous ownership can look like a disposal and an acquisition. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.
rationale: The DIL gives the field as a hashed ABN on the partnership tables, which record an individual's interest in an entity. The Australian Business Register publishes the ABN's format and issuer.

description_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions
value_definition: A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: the letter D followed by a two-digit division number, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
variable_description: The top level of the geographic coding of the person's usual address: whether that address is in geographic Australia at all. The ABS defines place of usual residence as "the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and AUSTP is the Australia (AUS) level of that coding, the coarsest of the geography columns on the 2021 person table alongside STEUCP, SA4UCP down to MBUCP for the same address. Its practical job is to isolate the overseas visitor, no usual address and migratory, off-shore and shipping cases before any finer geography is analysed.
description_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)
value_definition: The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS Main Structure, the top of the hierarchy that Mesh Blocks, SA1s to SA4s and states and territories aggregate into, together with the extra categories the usual residence coding carries: no usual address, migratory, off-shore and shipping, and overseas visitor (VVVV). There is no not stated code: an incomplete usual address is imputed, and IFPURP records that it was.
limitation: Being the top of the hierarchy, it separates almost nobody: nearly every person counted has a usual address in Australia, so a cross-tabulation on this column alone will look empty. It also records the address as at Census night 2021, not a residency test, so a person on a short overseas posting who kept an Australian usual address is coded in Australia.
rationale: The '(ur)' suffix and the person table identify this as the Australia level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence; the ABS Census Dictionary defines that concept and the ASGS Main Structure page defines the AUS level.

supersedes_rationale: The value domain read 'not specified' and 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' stood as both the value definition and the limitation, so the page never said that '(ur)' means usual residence or that AUST is a level of the ASGS.

evidence_quote: This variable records the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census.

value_domain: ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence five years ago
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)
variable_description: Whether the person's usual address five years before the Census was in Australia.
