value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Carer Allowance child identifier, ID number" (item 452), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_cda_child_id
variable_description: The child whose Carer Allowance is the reason a Health Care Card was issued. Carer Allowance goes to someone caring for a child with a disability or medical condition, and that arrangement brings a card with the child listed on it, so this column names which child. DSS defines it as "A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies whether there is a child in receipt of Carer Allowance". It is one of four child columns on ccd_hcc, each recording a different basis for a child appearing on the card, alongside the foster child, the other child and the dependent customer.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Carer Allowance child identifier, ID number" (item 452), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_cda_child_id
value_definition: A randomised numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits, drawn from the DSS person identifier domain. The digits are assigned by Centrelink and carry no information about the child.
limitation: It names the child by a Centrelink identifier rather than by the SYNTHETIC_AEUID that carries a record onto the PLIDA spine, so the column on its own will not take you to that child's Census, tax or health records. A blank also does not mean no Carer Allowance: it means no Carer Allowance child was listed on this card, and the allowance itself is recorded on the payment tables.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_cda_child_id to DSS data element 452, whose definition ties the identifier to Carer Allowance and whose value domain is the fifteen-digit person ID number.
evidence_quote: A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies whether there is a child in receipt of Carer Allowance.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Carer allowance child identifier" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying that the identifier is not a spine key.

value_domain: Count of children listed on a concession card
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Concession Card, Number of Listed Children" (item 458), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_child_id_list_count
variable_description: How many children were listed on the person's concession card, defined by DSS as "The maximum number of children listed on a concession card held by the card holder". The column appears on all four concession card tables, so the count always belongs to the card that table covers: Health Care Card in ccd_hcc, Pensioner Concession Card in ccd_pcc, low-income Health Care Card in ccd_hcc_lic and Seniors Health Card in ccd_shc. CONCESSION names the card type and CARD_START_DATE and CARD_END_DATE bound the period, so the count is the high-water mark over that period rather than a figure for any one day.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Concession Card, Number of Listed Children" (item 458), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_child_id_list_count
value_definition: A whole number in a five-digit field, format {NNNN}N, with 0 the default. DSS specifies it as a maximum over the card period, not a point-in-time count.
limitation: Being a maximum, it will exceed the number of children actually listed on any given day wherever children were added and removed, so it cannot be used as a family size on a date. Children listed for concession purposes are also not the same as children in the person's care: a child can be in care without being listed, and a listed child can be the partner's dependant.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_child_id_list_count to DSS data element 458, whose definition specifies the maximum rather than a current count, and whose value domain is a five-digit total number with 0 as default.
evidence_quote: The maximum number of children listed on a concession card held by the card holder
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Number of listed children" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding that the figure is a period maximum rather than a current count.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card dependent customer identifier, ID number" (item 54282), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_dep_customer_id
variable_description: The dependent adult listed on the person's Health Care Card, named by a Centrelink identifier. A dependent customer is someone who is themselves a Centrelink customer but whose concession flows from this card holder, most often a young person past the age at which they would be recorded as a child. DSS defines it as "A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies a dependent customer listed on a concession card". EXT_DOM_PARTNER_ID beside it records the partner, and the three child columns record children on their own basis for listing.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card dependent customer identifier, ID number" (item 54282), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_dep_customer_id
value_definition: A randomised numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits from the DSS person identifier domain, assigned by Centrelink and carrying no information about the person.
limitation: Dependency here is the concession test Centrelink applied, which is narrower than living together and narrower than financial support in any ordinary sense, so the column will miss adult children who were supported but not listed. The identifier is also not the SYNTHETIC_AEUID spine key, so the dependent person cannot be followed into other PLIDA datasets from this column.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_dep_customer_id to DSS data element 54282, which supplies the definition and the fifteen-digit person ID value domain.
evidence_quote: A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies a dependent customer listed on a concession card.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Dependent person identifier" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, leaving "dependent" undefined.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card foster child identifier, ID number" (item 251), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_fst_child_id
variable_description: The foster child listed on the person's Health Care Card. A carer can claim a Health Care Card on behalf of a child in their care, and DSS's own notes on the equivalent Snap-DOMINO flag say the carer does not need to be a formal foster carer for the child to be listed this way. The registry defines the identifier as "A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies a foster child listed on a concession card". It is one of four ways a child appears on the card, beside the Carer Allowance child, the other child and the dependent customer.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card foster child identifier, ID number" (item 251), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_fst_child_id
value_definition: A randomised numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits from the DSS person identifier domain, assigned by Centrelink.
limitation: A value shows a child was listed on a card as a foster child, not that a formal statutory placement existed, so the column is not a measure of out-of-home care. Only one identifier fits the field, so a carer with several children listed on this basis shows one of them here and a larger EXT_DOM_CHILD_ID_LIST_COUNT.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_fst_child_id to DSS data element 251, which gives the definition and the fifteen-digit person ID value domain, and the Snap-DOMINO card flag CARD_HEALTH_CARE_FST carries the custodian's note that formal foster care is not required.
evidence_quote: A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies a foster child listed on a concession card.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Foster child identifier" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, inviting the column to be read as a record of statutory foster placements.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Domino Household ID" (item 108241), bound to snap_domino_beta.dom_household_id
variable_description: The income unit the person belonged to on the snapshot date: either the person alone, or the person and their partner. DSS defines it as "A unique identifier used to identify a financial unit made up of a person and their partner", covering married, de facto and registered relationships, and the PLIDA data item list adds that the value is built by concatenating the person's DOMINO identifier with their partner's. Two partnered people therefore share one value, and PARTNERED_STATUS on the same row is the flag that says which of the two cases applies.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Domino Household ID" (item 108241), bound to snap_domino_beta.dom_household_id
value_definition: A numeric value of up to nineteen characters, formed from one or two DOMINO person identifiers. It carries no information about the unit beyond the identities it joins.
limitation: The unit is a couple for means-testing purposes, not a household or a dwelling, so it cannot be used to count household size or to reconstruct who lives together: children and other adults at the same address are outside it, and two units can share one address. The value also changes whenever a partnership starts or ends, so it is not a stable key for following a person over time.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds dom_household_id to DSS data element 108241, which defines the unit as a person and their partner for payment eligibility and gives the nineteen-character numeric format.
evidence_quote: A unique identifier used to identify a financial unit made up of a person and their partner
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's concatenation note but printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing warned a reader against reading the column as a household.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card other child identifier, ID number" (item 54281), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_oth_child_id
variable_description: A child listed on the person's Health Care Card who is neither a foster child nor the Carer Allowance child. DSS defines it as "A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies an 'other' child listed on a concession card", so it is the residual of the three child columns: a dependent child listed because the card holder receives Family Tax Benefit for them, or who otherwise meets the card's dependency test. CHILD_ID on the same row holds the listed children as text and EXT_DOM_CHILD_ID_LIST_COUNT how many there were over the card period.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card other child identifier, ID number" (item 54281), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_oth_child_id
value_definition: A randomised numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits from the DSS person identifier domain, assigned by Centrelink.
limitation: "Other" is defined by what it is not, so a value says a child was listed without saying on what basis; the reason has to be inferred from ENT_TYPE and REASON_CODE on the same row. Only one identifier fits the field, so a card listing several such children shows one of them.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_oth_child_id to DSS data element 54281, which names the residual category explicitly and gives the fifteen-digit person ID value domain.
evidence_quote: A randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies an 'other' child listed on a concession card.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Other child identifier" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying what "other" is other than.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card partner identifier, ID number" (item 441), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_partner_id
variable_description: The partner listed on the person's concession card, named by a Centrelink identifier. DSS defines it as "A numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies the partner of a recipient on a concession card". It appears on all four card tables — Health Care Card, Pensioner Concession Card, low-income Health Care Card and Seniors Health Card — and is what makes a card a couple's rather than an individual's. A change of value between rows for one person is a change of partner, and a value appearing or disappearing marks a partnership starting or ending as far as the card is concerned.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Concession card partner identifier, ID number" (item 441), bound to ccd_hcc.ext_dom_partner_id
value_definition: A numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits from the DSS person identifier domain, assigned by Centrelink.
limitation: Listing a partner on a card is a concession decision, not a relationship record, so this column will miss partners who were never listed and will keep a partner on the card until the card is updated. The relationship tables, rlt_cust_ptnr_list in particular, are where partnering history belongs. The identifier is also not the SYNTHETIC_AEUID spine key, so the partner cannot be followed into other PLIDA datasets from here.
rationale: CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) binds ext_dom_partner_id to DSS data element 441, which gives the definition and the fifteen-digit person ID value domain, and the same column appears on the other three concession card tables in the registry.
evidence_quote: A numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies the partner of a recipient on a concession card.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Partner listed identifier" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell whether the column was a relationship record or a card record.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Relationship identifier, ID number" (item 473), bound to the DOMINO relationship tables
variable_description: The other person in the relationship the row records, defined by DSS as "The ID of a recipient the client has a relationship with, as represented by a randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink". Which relationship that is depends on the table: a partner in rlt_cust_ptnr_list, a parent or child in rlt_parent_child_list, a grandparent or grandchild in the two grandparent tables, and the child a person is principal carer for in rlt_prin_carer_beta. REL_CODE names the type — married, de facto, parent, child, sibling, guardian, ward and so on — and REL_QUAL_CODE qualifies it, so this column is the who and those two are the what.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Relationship identifier, ID number" (item 473), bound to the DOMINO relationship tables
value_definition: A randomised numeric identifier of up to fifteen digits from the DSS person identifier domain. The digits are assigned by Centrelink and carry no information about the person.
limitation: It names the related person by a Centrelink identifier rather than by SYNTHETIC_AEUID, so the column on its own will not take you to that person's Census, tax or health records. Relationships are also recorded because they affect payment, so a family tie that never mattered to a claim never appears, and the absence of a row is not evidence that the relationship did not exist.
rationale: RLT_CUST_PTNR_LIST_EXT and RLT_PARENT_CHILD_LIST (PLIDA) both bind ext_dom_rel_id to DSS data element 473, whose definition names it as the identifier of the related recipient and whose value domain is the fifteen-digit person ID number. Data element 375 supplies the relationship type codes on the same rows.
evidence_quote: The ID of a recipient the client has a relationship with, as represented by a randomised numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Relationship person id" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying that the relationship differs by table.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: First Active ISP" (item 108857), bound to snap_domino_beta.first_active_isp
variable_description: Which income support payment the person was on when their current unbroken run of income support began. Snap-DOMINO builds that run by joining spells across short breaks, so this is the payment that opened the period bounded by ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE, not the payment the person is on at the snapshot. Read with LAST_ACTIVE_ISP, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP it shows how someone moved between payments inside a single spell of support, which is the usual pattern for a person who goes from a student payment to unemployment and then to a parenting payment.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: First Active ISP" (item 108857), bound to snap_domino_beta.first_active_isp
value_definition: A three or four letter code, format AAA{A}, from the 95-value DSS benefit type code list: JSP for JobSeeker Payment, AGE for Age Pension, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS and PPP for the two parenting payments, and UNK where the payment is unknown.
limitation: It resets every time a break longer than the tolerance ends a run, so for a person with a long and interrupted history it is a recent fact rather than a first-ever payment. It also gives one payment where a person can hold several at once, so the supplement or family payment they also received at that moment is not visible here.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds first_active_isp to DSS data element 108857, which publishes the benefit type code value domain and its AAA{A} format, and binds the active period start and end dates that define the run this payment opens.
evidence_quote: First payment in active Income Support Payment period
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying that the code set is the DSS benefit type list or that the run tolerates gaps.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Family Tax Benefit Part A on Snap" (item 108812), bound to snap_domino_beta.ftba_on_snap
variable_description: Whether the person was receiving Family Tax Benefit Part A on the snapshot date itself. Family Tax Benefit Part A is the per-child family payment, so a Y marks a family with a dependent child on the single day SNAP_DATE names. It is the point-in-time counterpart to FTBA_PANEL_DAYS, which counts days across the whole panel period, and FTBA_TYPE_CODE and FTBA_BEN_STATUS on the same row say which variant of the payment and whether the entitlement was current, suspended or cancelled.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Family Tax Benefit Part A on Snap" (item 108812), bound to snap_domino_beta.ftba_on_snap
value_definition: A single letter from the DSS yes/no/missing domain: Y where the benefit was received on the snapshot date and N otherwise, with N as the default value.
limitation: A one-day flag misses anyone whose entitlement started the day after or ended the day before, so a family with most of a year on Family Tax Benefit shows N if the snapshot fell in a gap. The flag is also about receipt on the day, not the amount, so it does not separate a family on the maximum rate from one on a small residual entitlement.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds ftba_on_snap to DSS data element 108812, whose value domain is the yes/no/missing code with N as the default, and binds ftba_panel_days, ftba_type_code and ftba_ben_status on the same row.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating FTBA benefit received on snap date
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so the Y/N domain and the single-day risk were both undocumented.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Family Tax Benefit Part A panel days" (item 108808), bound to snap_domino_beta.ftba_panel_days
variable_description: How many days in the panel period the person was active on Family Tax Benefit Part A. It is the duration counterpart to FTBA_ON_SNAP, which covers a single day, so the two answer different questions: how long, and whether on the day. A positive count with N on the snapshot flag is the common and informative case — a family that had Family Tax Benefit during the period but not on SNAP_DATE.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Family Tax Benefit Part A panel days" (item 108808), bound to snap_domino_beta.ftba_panel_days
value_definition: A whole number of days in an eight-digit count field, with 0 the default value.
limitation: The count is bounded by the panel window the extract covers, so it is not lifetime days on the payment and cannot be compared between people whose panels differ in length. Days active also means days with a current determination rather than days paid, so a period of suspension can still add to the count.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds ftba_panel_days to DSS data element 108808, whose value domain is Count N(8) with 0 as the default and whose data element concept is "Payment: Active days".
evidence_quote: Number of days active on FTBA benefit
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without distinguishing days on a determination from days paid.

value_domain: Greater Capital City Statistical Area name (ASGS 2011)
value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Greater Capital City Statistical Area (GCCSA 2011), Name" (item 110035), bound to snap_domino_beta.gccsa
variable_description: The Greater Capital City Statistical Area of the person's accommodation address on the snapshot date, held as a name rather than a code. DSS titles the data element "Address: Greater Capital City Statistical Area (GCCSA 2011), Name", so it is on the 2011 edition of the statistical geography while MESHBLOCK, SA2, SA3, SA4 and LGA on the same row are on the 2021 edition; the boundaries beside each other are a decade apart. The classification splits each state into its greater capital city and the rest of the state, which is the coarsest division in the ASGS above state level.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Greater Capital City Statistical Area (GCCSA 2011), Name" (item 110035), bound to snap_domino_beta.gccsa
value_definition: A text name of up to thirty characters from the 2011 Greater Capital City Statistical Area classification, such as Greater Sydney or Rest of NSW, with NA where none applies.
limitation: Because it is a name on a 2011 edition, it will not join to a GCCSA code table or to the 2021-based geography on the same row without a concordance, and the areas it names are not identical to their 2021 successors. It also describes the address Centrelink held, which is the address the person last reported, so it lags a move rather than tracking one.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds gccsa to DSS data element 110035, whose title fixes the 2011 edition and whose value domain is a thirty-character alphabetic name with NA as the only listed value, while the neighbouring geography columns bind to 2021 ASGS code elements.
evidence_quote: Describes the Greater Capital City Statistical Area (GCCSA) for accommodation address of a person or Income Unit.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and nothing on the page warned that this column is an older edition of the geography than the columns beside it.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data elements "Person: Sex/gender, Code" (item 109686) and "Person - Sex/Gender, Code A" (item 68820), bound to snap_domino_beta.gender and static_demogs.gender
variable_description: The person's sex or gender as Centrelink records it, coded differently in the two DOMINO tables that carry the column. On static_demogs the codes are M, F, X for other and U for unknown. On snap_domino_beta the same column has been collapsed: DSS states that "Where a stated gender is not male or female it has been coded to female", so F there means female or non-binary. A count of people recorded as other than male or female is therefore possible from one table and impossible from the other.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data elements "Person: Sex/gender, Code" (item 109686) and "Person - Sex/Gender, Code A" (item 68820), bound to snap_domino_beta.gender and static_demogs.gender
value_definition: A single letter. In static_demogs: M male, F female, X other, U unknown. In snap_domino_beta: M male, F female or non-binary, with U as a supplementary unknown.
limitation: The value follows what the person told Centrelink at some point and is not systematically refreshed, so it lags a change in recorded gender rather than tracking it. Because Snap-DOMINO folds non-binary responses into F, the two tables will disagree for those people and a person's recorded value can change between tables without their gender having changed.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds gender to data element 109686, whose definition states the collapsing rule and whose value domain gives M, F and supplementary U. STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA) binds the same column name to data element 68820, whose value domain gives M, F, X and U.
evidence_quote: The gender identification of a person is represented by a code in Snap Domino. Where a stated gender is not male or female it has been coded to female.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Recipient gender" with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, concealing that the two tables use different code sets and that one of them cannot represent a non-binary response.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient—impairment rating, NN[N] (%)" (item 616), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_rate
variable_description: The total impairment rating assigned to a person's medical conditions at a work capacity assessment, which DSS defines as "the impairment rating for a recipient's medical condition(s), expressed as a percentage in 5% increments". It is the sum across conditions rather than any one condition's score; IMPRMT_CODE on the same row carries the per-condition rating, and IMPRMT_VER_DATE the day that version of the assessment became current. Twenty points is the level at which Disability Support Pension becomes reachable, which is why the distribution of this column clusters rather than spreading smoothly.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient—impairment rating, NN[N] (%)" (item 616), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_rate
value_definition: A whole number in a field of up to three digits, awarded in five-point steps. The companion code list runs 0 no functional impact, 5 mild, 10 moderate, 20 severe and 30 extreme, with the intermediate values and everything up to 95 also permitted.
limitation: A rating exists only where an assessment was done, so a blank means no assessment rather than no impairment, and the rated population is skewed towards people claiming Disability Support Pension. The rating measures functional impact on work capacity rather than diagnosis or clinical severity, so two people with the same condition can score very differently and a high score is not a measure of how ill someone is.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds imprmt_rate to DSS data element 616, which gives the definition and the five-point increment rule, and binds imprmt_code beside it to data element 65080, whose value list supplies the functional-impact labels for 0, 5, 10, 20 and 30.
evidence_quote: the impairment rating for a recipient's medical condition(s), expressed as a percentage in 5% increments
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Impairment rating" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know the scale, the increment or that a blank means no assessment.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Medical Assessment: Record Start Date, DD-MM-YYYY" (item 59541), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_ver_date
variable_description: The day the version of the impairment assessment on this row became current, which DSS defines as "The particular day on which the record of a medical assessment became current". The mcd_dtls table keeps a history, so a person reassessed after a change in condition has several rows and this date is what orders them: the rating in IMPRMT_RATE belongs to the version starting here. It is a record-keeping date, distinct from PERIOD_START_DATE, which bounds the reporting episode the row was extracted in.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Medical Assessment: Record Start Date, DD-MM-YYYY" (item 59541), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_ver_date
value_definition: A calendar date in a ten-character field. DSS specifies the format as DD-MM-YYYY, which is the reverse of the YYYY-MM-DD used by the period and incapacity dates on the same table.
limitation: It dates the record, not the examination or the onset of the condition, so it sits after the medical evidence it summarises and can move when an assessment is corrected. It cannot be used to date the start of impairment: a condition present for twenty years but first assessed in 2015 carries a 2015 date.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds imprmt_ver_date to DSS data element 59541, whose definition makes it a record currency date and whose value domain is DD-MM-YYYY, while the neighbouring date columns on the same table bind to YYYY-MM-DD elements.
evidence_quote: The particular day on which the record of a medical assessment became current.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Impairment version date" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without noting the different date format or that it is a record date.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 642), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_end
variable_description: The day a certified period of temporary incapacity ended, which DSS defines as "The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition ends". Incapacity here is the medical-certificate arrangement that suspends a person's mutual obligation requirements while they cannot work or study, so the period matters for whether a payment could be suspended. INCAP_START is the other end of the same period, INCAP_EXEMPT records whether an exemption was actually granted, and INCAP_WK_WRK_HRS how many hours a week the certifying doctor still thought the person able to work.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 642), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_end
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters. DSS's definition writes the same date as YYYYMMDD while the value domain gives the hyphenated form.
limitation: It is the end date the certificate specified, not the day the person recovered or returned to work, and a certificate superseded early still carries its original end date. Successive certificates for one illness appear as separate periods, so the length of an illness is not the length of any one period and has to be built by joining consecutive rows.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_end to DSS data element 642, which supplies the definition and the YYYY-MM-DD value domain, and binds incap_start, incap_exempt and incap_wk_wrk_hrs on the same row.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition ends, expressed as YYYYMMDD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity period end date" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without explaining what incapacity means administratively or that the date is a certificate date.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity exemption indicator, Code" (item 654), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_exempt
variable_description: Whether the person was granted an exemption from mutual obligation requirements on the ground of incapacity, which DSS defines as an indicator of "whether an incapacity exemption has been granted or not". A medical certificate covering INCAP_START to INCAP_END does not by itself excuse a person; a delegate has to grant the exemption, and this flag records that decision. It matters because an exemption stops participation requirements and the payment suspensions that follow from missing them.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity exemption indicator, Code" (item 654), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_exempt
value_definition: A single letter: Y where the exemption was granted, N where it was not. DSS publishes the two codes as "Incapacity Exemption Granted" and "Incapacity Exemption Not Granted".
limitation: An N is a decision recorded against this period, not evidence that the person was well, and the flag does not say why an exemption was refused. It covers exemption on incapacity grounds only, so a person exempted for another reason — a major personal crisis, caring responsibilities, a natural disaster — still shows N here.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_exempt to DSS data element 654, whose value domain publishes the two codes with their meanings and whose definition names the granting decision.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether an incapacity exemption has been granted or not.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity exemption indicator" and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, although a published two-value code list exists.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 641), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_start
variable_description: The day a certified period of temporary incapacity began, which DSS defines as "The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition commences". It opens the period that INCAP_END closes, and the pair is what makes this table a history of episodes of ill health among income support recipients rather than a static medical record. INCAP_EXEMPT says whether the period produced an exemption from requirements and INCAP_WK_WRK_HRS what residual work capacity the doctor certified.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 641), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_start
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters. DSS's definition writes the same date as YYYYMMDD while the value domain gives the hyphenated form.
limitation: It dates the certified period, not the onset of the illness: a person who was unwell for months before seeing a doctor about their payment obligations starts here on the day the certificate begins. The column also only exists where incapacity was reported to Centrelink, so it measures illness that interfered with a claim rather than illness in the population.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_start to DSS data element 641, which gives the definition and the YYYY-MM-DD value domain, and pairs it with incap_end on the same row.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of incapacity relating to a recipient's medical condition commences, expressed as YYYYMMDD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity period start date" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity adjusted weekly work hours, Total number" (item 657), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_wk_wrk_hrs
variable_description: The weekly hours the certifying doctor considered the person still able to work during a period of incapacity, which DSS defines as "The number of hours per week that the issuing doctor considers the client able to work". It is what separates partial from total incapacity: a person certified for some hours can be held to reduced requirements rather than exempted outright, which is why it sits beside INCAP_EXEMPT. The hours apply to the period bounded by INCAP_START and INCAP_END.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Incapacity adjusted weekly work hours, Total number" (item 657), bound to mcd_dtls.incap_wk_wrk_hrs
value_definition: A whole number of hours per week in a two-digit field, so 0 to 99, with a full stop as the missing marker.

A zero means certified as able to work no hours, which is a positive finding rather than a gap, and confusing it with the missing marker turns full incapacity into no data.
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) binds incap_wk_wrk_hrs to DSS data element 657, whose definition attributes the figure to the issuing doctor and whose value domain is a two-digit total number with a full stop for missing.
evidence_quote: The number of hours per week that the issuing doctor considers the client able to work.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Incapacity adjusted work hours" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying whose judgement the hours are or that zero differs from missing.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Indigenous status, Code" (item 461), bound to indg_stat.indig_code
variable_description: Whether the person identified as Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander or South Sea Islander in their dealings with Centrelink, defined by DSS as "Whether a person identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, as represented by a code". The indg_stat table holds nothing but this column and the person key, because DSS treats the item as sensitive and releases it separately from the rest of the demographic data. The code set is wider than the ABS standard question: it separates South Sea Islander origin, records where a person declined to answer, and marks where an ATO customer was never asked.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Indigenous status, Code" (item 461), bound to indg_stat.indig_code
value_definition: A single letter from a thirteen-value list: A Aboriginal, T Torres Strait Islander, B both, S South Sea Islander, with C, E and F combining South Sea Islander with the others, G South Sea Islander only, N none of them, D and H for declining to answer, and X and Z where an ATO customer was not asked. DSS groups A, B, C, E, F and T as Indigenous, and blank, D, G, H, N, S, X and Z as not identified as Indigenous.
limitation: It is administrative self-identification captured at some point of contact with Centrelink, not a Census response, so it is missing for anyone who never had reason to answer and is not refreshed when a person's identification changes. The "not identified" grouping mixes people who said no with people who declined and people who were never asked, so treating it as a non-Indigenous count overstates that group and understates Indigenous status.
rationale: Indigenous Status - sensitive (PLIDA) binds indg_status.indig_code to DSS data element 461, which publishes the full thirteen-code value domain and the two supplementary groupings, and shows the table carries only this column and the person key.
evidence_quote: Whether a person identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only "Recipient indigenous code" and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, although DSS publishes the complete code list and the Indigenous grouping rule.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108889), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_end_date
variable_description: The last day of the person's unbroken run on income support, where Snap-DOMINO's definition of unbroken tolerates short exits. DSS allows gaps of up to six weeks where the whole period including gaps is under a year, and up to thirteen weeks where it is longer, so this date can sit well after several brief departures from payment. LAST_ACTIVE_ISP names the payment the run ended on, and ISP_PANEL_DAYS counts the days actually spent on payment within the panel.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108889), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_end_date
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters.
limitation: Subtracting the start date from this one measures the run including its tolerated gaps, so it overstates time on payment; ISP_PANEL_DAYS is the column that counts days actually received. An end date at or near the snapshot also does not establish that the person left income support, because a run still open when the extract was drawn has to be read against SNAP_DATE and ISP_ON_SNAP.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds isp_active_end_date to DSS data element 108889, whose definition sets out the six-week and thirteen-week gap tolerances and whose value domain is a ten-character YYYY-MM-DD date.
evidence_quote: End of an active Income Support Payment period, allowing for gaps of up to 6 weeks if the total period (including gaps) is under one year, and up to 13 weeks if over one year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing warned against reading the interval as time on payment.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108888), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_start_date
variable_description: The first day of the person's current unbroken run on income support. Snap-DOMINO builds the run by joining spells across short breaks — up to six weeks where the whole period is under a year, up to thirteen weeks where it is longer — so the date reaches back past exits that a spell-based measure would treat as the end of a claim. FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP names the payment the run opened on, which need not be the payment the person is on at the snapshot.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: ISP Active Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD" (item 108888), bound to snap_domino_beta.isp_active_start_date
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD, ten characters.
limitation: It is the start of the current run, not the person's first contact with income support: a break longer than the tolerance resets it, so a long history can appear as a recent start and duration measures built from this column understate lifetime receipt. It also cannot be used to date a job loss, because a run can open on a student, carer or parenting payment rather than an unemployment one.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds isp_active_start_date to DSS data element 108888, whose definition sets out the gap tolerances and the intended use in identifying people struggling to find work, and whose value domain is a ten-character YYYY-MM-DD date.
evidence_quote: Start of an active period on an Income Support Payment
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation, without saying that the date resets after a long break.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108846, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap'
variable_description: Says whether the person was being paid an income support payment on the day the snapshot was taken. It is the flag that turns Snap DOMINO into a point-in-time count of income support recipients: SNAP_DATE gives the day, ISP_TYPE_CODE names which payment, ISP_BEN_STATUS gives its status, and ISP_PANEL_DAYS counts activity over the surrounding window rather than on the day alone. Read it beside the parallel FTBA_ON_SNAP, FTBB_ON_SNAP, RENT_ON_SNAP and SUP_ON_SNAP flags, which cover family payments, rent assistance and supplements on the same date.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108846, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap'
value_definition: One character from the DSS yes/no/missing code domain: Y for received on the snapshot date, N for not. The domain admits a missing value as well, so a person with no income support record at all need not read as N.
limitation: A day is not a year. Someone paid for eleven months who happened to be off payment on the snapshot date reads as N, so the flag understates how many people touch income support over a period. It also carries no amount, and it does not separate a full-rate entitlement from one reduced to nil by the income test.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry binds the snap_domino_beta column isp_on_snap to the data element 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap', which publishes both the definition and the yes/no/missing value domain.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating Income Support Payment received on snap date
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the data item list wording as its whole description and repeated 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing said what a snapshot flag measures or what it misses.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108845, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days'
variable_description: Counts the days the person spent active on an income support payment across the panel window the snapshot belongs to, rather than on the snapshot day itself. It is what separates someone continuously on payment from someone who cycled on and off between snapshots, which the ISP_ON_SNAP flag cannot show. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE bound the underlying spell, and DOMINO treats that spell as tolerating breaks of up to six weeks where the whole period runs under a year.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108845, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days'
value_definition: An integer count of days in the registry's Count N(8) domain, with a published default of 0. Days are summed across income support payments of any type, so the total measures time on income support rather than time on one payment.
limitation: The total cannot tell you which payment the days belonged to, so a move from JobSeeker Payment to Disability Support Pension inside the window collapses into a single number and only ISP_TYPE_CODE, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP separate them. Because 0 is the default, a genuine zero and a person with no income support history look identical.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry binds snap_domino_beta.isp_panel_days to 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days' and publishes its Count N(8) domain and its default of 0. The registry does not publish the length of the panel window, so that part of the description is read off the snapshot design rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Number of days active on Income Support Payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so a reader could not tell what period the days were counted over.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'
variable_description: The income support payment the person was on at the close of the active payment spell that the snapshot falls in. With FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP it brackets the spell, so a row shows where a period on income support started and where it finished without joining to the payment history tables. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE give the dates of that spell, which DOMINO builds by stitching over breaks of up to six weeks.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which runs to about a hundred values: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS for Parenting Payment Single.
limitation: It names the last payment inside one stitched spell, not the last payment a person ever received, so a person who returns to income support after a longer break starts a new spell with its own closing payment. The column also gives no date for the change and no reason for it.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.last_active_isp to 'Payment: Last Active ISP' and gives its value domain as the DSS benefit type code, the same code set used by ISP_TYPE_CODE, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP.
evidence_quote: Last payment in active Income Support Payment period
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, leaving the benefit type code set undocumented.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108688, 'Address: Local Government Area (ASGS 2021), Code NNNNN'
variable_description: The council area the person's address fell in on the snapshot date. The DSS registry defines it as "The designated region representing the whole geographical area of responsibility of an incorporated Local Government entity in which a given address is located, as represented by a code", which makes it the one geography on the snapshot table that matches an actual unit of government rather than a statistical area. It is the natural join for council-level service planning, while SA2, SA3 and SA4 on the same row are the ABS statistical alternatives.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108688, 'Address: Local Government Area (ASGS 2021), Code NNNNN'
value_definition: A code of up to five characters from the Local Government Areas (LGA) Code (2021) value domain, the ASGS code set for the council area a location belongs to.
limitation: LGAs do not nest inside the SA3 or SA4 codes beside them, and not every value is a council: where no incorporated local government exists the ABS codes the area as Unincorporated followed by the state or territory, which covers the whole of the Australian Capital Territory, northern South Australia and some other territories. Council amalgamations also retire and mint codes, so an LGA time series breaks where boundaries were redrawn.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.lga to the ASGS 2021 Local Government Area data element and publishes both the definition and the five-character 2021 LGA value domain.
evidence_quote: The designated region representing the whole geographical area of responsibility of an incorporated Local Government entity in which a given address is located, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Local government area' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no edition, no code width and no warning about unincorporated areas.

variable_description: The mesh block the person's address fell in, on the derived location table that holds one row per address episode. The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", so this is the finest geography DOMINO publishes and everything else on the row aggregates from it. SA1_ASGS_2021, SA2_ASGS_2021, SA4_ASGS_2021 and STATE_ASGS_2021 are the same address at coarser levels, ARID_HASH_TRUNC identifies the address itself, and START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period the person was there.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS 2021 mesh block code, format N(11), whose leading digit is the state or territory. Mesh blocks nest exactly inside SA1s, so the SA1 column on the same row is a strict aggregation of this one.
limitation: The ABS designs a mesh block to hold roughly 30 to 60 dwellings, so it is a small area, not a dwelling or a household: two people sharing a code are neighbours and need not live together. Boundaries were redrawn between ASGS editions, so a 2021 code cannot be compared with the differently coded MESHBLOCK column in loc_dtls without a correspondence file.
rationale: The registry lists mb_asgs_2021 as a column of the LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA) distribution and maps it to the ASGS 2021 Meshblock data element, which publishes the ABS definition and the N(11) value domain.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no code width, no nesting rule and no warning that a mesh block is not a household.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 635, 'Recipient: Secondary medical condition identifier, ID number'
variable_description: Links a secondary medical condition record to the earlier record it replaced, so the condition history reads as a sequence of corrections rather than as a set of separate conditions. The DSS registry defines it as "An identifier that links a medical condition that has been overwritten". It sits on the medical conditions details table beside MED_SCNDRY_GRP, which names the condition group, and MED_SCNDRY_PERM, which records how lasting the condition was judged to be.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 635, 'Recipient: Secondary medical condition identifier, ID number'
value_definition: A short number, one or two digits, from the registry's Secondary medical condition ID number domain, which auto-increments from 1. It distinguishes successive versions of a record rather than naming a condition.
limitation: The number carries no clinical meaning and cannot be used to identify or count conditions; MED_SCNDRY_GRP is the column that names what the condition was. Its absence means no record was overwritten, not that the person had no secondary condition, so treating a populated value as evidence of a second diagnosis double counts corrections as conditions.
rationale: The registry maps mcd_dtls.med_scndry_id to the Secondary medical condition identifier data element and publishes both its definition and the auto-incrementing N[N] domain. How the counter is scoped within a person's record is inferred from the auto-increment rule rather than stated.
evidence_quote: An identifier that links a medical condition that has been overwritten.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Secondary medical code identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have read it as a diagnosis code.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 230, 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code'
variable_description: Records how lasting the medical condition on this row was judged to be, which is the assessment that decides whether a condition can support a Disability Support Pension claim. The DSS registry binds the column to a data element defined as "The permanency of a recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code", and its five codes separate a permanent condition that has been diagnosed, treated and stabilised from one that is recurring or temporary. PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the assessment, and IMPRMT_RATE on the same table carries the impairment rating that goes with it.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 230, 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code'
value_definition: One character from the DSS permanency code set: D for permanent, diagnosed, treated and stabilised; P for permanent, not diagnosed, treated and stabilised; M for permanent; R for recurring; T for temporary.
limitation: Permanency here is an administrative judgement made for payment purposes, not a clinical prognosis, and a T does not mean a doctor expected recovery. The registry also ties this column to the primary condition data element while the PLIDA data item list calls it secondary, so check it against MED_PRMY_GRP and MED_SCNDRY_GRP before assuming which condition it qualifies.
rationale: The MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps med_scndry_perm to 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code', which publishes the definition and the five-value permanency code domain. The naming mismatch between the registry and the data item list is unresolved, which is why the confidence is medium.
evidence_quote: The permanency of a recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Secondary medical code pemanent indicator' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, implying a yes-or-no flag when the domain has five graded codes.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'
variable_description: The mesh block the address Centrelink held for the person fell in, one row per address period on the location details table. The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", so it is the finest location DOMINO records for a person. MESHMATCH beside it says whether the code came from matching the address itself or only its coordinates, SA1_MAINCODE, SA2_MAINCODE, POSTCODE and STATE are the same address at coarser levels, and the column repeats on the temporary and terminated address table and on snap_domino_beta.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'
value_definition: An eleven-digit mesh block code. The PLIDA data item list labels this column ASGS 2016 while the DSS registry maps it to the ASGS 2021 mesh block data element, so confirm the edition against the extract's reference period before joining to boundary files.
limitation: A mesh block is not a dwelling or a household, so two people with the same code live in the same small area rather than the same home. The code also describes where Centrelink last recorded the person, so it lags an unreported move, and where MESHMATCH is blank the address never matched at all and the geography columns on the row are empty rather than wrong.
rationale: The LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps meshblock to the ASGS 2021 Meshblock data element, which publishes the ABS definition and the N(11) domain. The edition disagreement with the PLIDA data item list is why the confidence is medium rather than high.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Asgs 2016 meshblock' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention that the DSS registry now maps the same column to the 2021 standard.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54357, 'Address: Meshblock matched indicator, Code'
variable_description: Says how the mesh block on the same row was derived: from the address text, or from the coordinates behind it. The DSS registry defines it as an "Indicator identifying if a meshblock code was matched by address or longitude/latitude coordinates", which makes it the quality flag for every geography column on the location details table. It matters because a coordinate match can put a record on the wrong side of a boundary, so MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE are less reliable at fine resolution where this column reads L.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54357, 'Address: Meshblock matched indicator, Code'
value_definition: One character: A where the mesh block was matched by address and L where it was matched by latitude and longitude. A blank is the registry's supplementary value, meaning the address was not matched at all.
limitation: It grades how the geocode was obtained, not whether the address was correct, so a stale or mistyped address that geocodes cleanly still returns A. It also says nothing about whether the person actually lived there, only about the matching step that produced the codes.
rationale: The registry maps loc_dtls.meshmatch to the Meshblock matched indicator data element, which publishes the definition, the A and L permissible values and the blank supplementary value.
evidence_quote: Indicator identifying if a meshblock code was matched by address or longitude/latitude coordinates.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so the two codes and their consequence for boundary accuracy went unstated.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'
variable_description: The month the person was born, held separately from YEAR_OF_BIRTH because the PLIDA release of DOMINO carries no full date of birth. The department's internal equivalent of this table, stt_pit_ext, holds a single date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD; the PLIDA version splits it into month and year, which is a disclosure control rather than a difference in what was collected. Combined with YEAR_OF_BIRTH it fixes a person's age to within a month, and AGE on the same row gives their age as at the extract date.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'
value_definition: A calendar month. The DSS registry restricts the metadata for this column, so neither the coding, the width nor the treatment of missing values is published, and the value should be inspected in the extract before use.
limitation: There is no day of birth, so an exact age on a given date cannot be calculated and anyone whose birthday falls in the month of an event sits on either side of an age threshold with equal probability. That matters for payments with sharp age tests, such as the move from Youth Allowance to JobSeeker Payment or reaching Age Pension age, where a month of uncertainty is enough to misclassify eligibility.
rationale: The registry's STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA) distribution lists month_of_birth and year_of_birth as columns but marks their data elements permission restricted, while the internal stt_pit_ext distribution for the same table lists a single date_of_birth field. That supports what the column is and why it exists, but publishes nothing about its value domain, so the status stays guessed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Birth month' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that the split from a full date of birth is the reason exact ages cannot be built.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108855, 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment'
variable_description: The income support payment the person moves onto next within the same active payment spell. With PREV_ISP it lets one snapshot row be read as a transition rather than a state: Parenting Payment Single to JobSeeker Payment as a youngest child ages out, or JobSeeker Payment to Disability Support Pension after a successful claim. Where the current payment is the last in the spell there is nothing to point to, and LAST_ACTIVE_ISP names the closing payment instead.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108855, 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment'
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which covers about a hundred payments: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, CAR for Carer Payment.
limitation: The next payment is scoped to the current spell, so a payment taken up after a break too long to be stitched into that spell never appears here. The column also carries no date, so it says a transition happened without saying when, and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE bounds the whole spell rather than the changeover.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.next_isp to 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment' and gives its value domain as the DSS benefit type code. That the field is empty at the end of a spell follows from the definition's scoping to the period of activity rather than being stated on the page.

supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the benefit type code set or the spell scoping that decides when the field is empty.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'
variable_description: Says what kind of entity the demographic record describes: a person, a child, or an organisation. The DSS registry defines the column as containing "the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer", and it matters because DOMINO's customer records are not all adults with a claim of their own. Children listed on a carer's or a family payment record, and organisations acting as nominees or payees, sit in the same customer table, so this is the column that keeps them out of a count of recipients.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'
value_definition: A three-character code with three permissible values: PER, CHI and ORG. The registry publishes the codes without written meanings, so the expansions to person, child and organisation come from the code letters themselves.
limitation: It classifies the record, not a person's role in a payment: a CHI record does not say which payment the child was listed against or who claimed for them, and the relationship tables carry that link. Filtering to PER is also not the same as filtering to adults, because the object type follows how the record was created rather than the person's age now.
rationale: The registry maps static_demogs.object_type_code to 'Recipient: Object Type, Code' and publishes the three-value domain. The expansion of each code and the caution about age are read from the code letters and the table's contents rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Contains the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Object type code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the domain has exactly three values and decides whether a row is a recipient at all.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108240, 'Partnered status'
variable_description: Says whether Centrelink had the person recorded as a member of a couple on the snapshot date. Partnered status drives rates, income tests and asset tests across almost every payment, so it explains rate differences on the snapshot table that ISP_TYPE_CODE alone cannot. EXT_DOM_HOUSEHOLD_ID pairs the person with their partner by concatenating the two DOMINO person identifiers, so a Y here should sit beside a two-person household identifier.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108240, 'Partnered status'
value_definition: One alphabetic character: Y for partnered and N for not partnered, with U as the registry's supplementary value for unknown. Three states can therefore appear.
limitation: It is a social security assessment of whether a couple relationship exists, not a marital status, so a de facto couple reads as Y and a married couple who have separated under one roof can read as N. It also refers only to the snapshot date and says nothing about how long the relationship had been recorded or how often it changed.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.partnered_status to the 'Partnered status' data element and publishes the Y and N permissible values plus the U supplementary value.
evidence_quote: The active partnership status of a person, represented by a flag.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the unknown code and the difference between assessed couple status and marital status were both missing.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 615, 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The date a person's blindness was diagnosed, which is the qualifying date for the blind rate of Age Pension or Disability Support Pension. The DSS registry defines it as "The date upon which a recipient's blindness was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". It is the only medical field on the static demographics table, and it belongs there rather than in the dated medical condition records because blind status is assessed once and then attaches to the person.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 615, 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. It is populated only for recipients assessed as permanently blind, so it is empty for almost every person on the table.
limitation: A populated date means blindness was diagnosed, not that the person was paid a blind pension from that date or paid at all; claim, grant and rate information sit in the payment history tables. It is also not an onset date, since it records the ophthalmologist's diagnosis rather than when sight was lost, and those can be years apart.
rationale: The registry maps static_demogs.pen_blind_start_date to 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD' and publishes its definition and the YYYY-MM-DD date domain.
evidence_quote: The date upon which a recipient's blindness was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Recipient pension blindness start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying who makes the assessment or that the date is a diagnosis rather than an onset.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 428, 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code'
variable_description: Says whether the concession card determination on this row was still pending rather than settled. The DSS registry defines it as an indicator of "whether a concession card is pending", so it is what separates a card the person actually held from a determination still in progress. It appears on all four concession card tables, covering the Health Care Card, the Pensioner Concession Card, the low income card and the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, and it should be read with CARD_ISSUE_DATE, CARD_START_DATE and CARD_END_DATE, because a pending row can carry a start date before any card was produced.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 428, 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code'
value_definition: One character, Y or N, with N as the registry's default. The field is boolean, so a row carrying no explicit value is treated as not pending.
limitation: It records the state of the determination when the row was written, not the eventual outcome, so a pending row is not evidence that the card was later granted or refused. Counting card holders without excluding pending rows overstates coverage, and the flag cannot tell you how long the determination stayed pending.
rationale: The CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps pending_flag to 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code', which publishes the definition, the Y and N values and the N default.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether a concession card is pending.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Concession card pending flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that including pending rows inflates a count of card holders.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 394, 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the record on this row stops applying, closing an episode that PERIOD_START_DATE opened. The DSS registry defines it as "The date on which a reporting period relating to an event ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". Nearly every DOMINO table is built this way, with one row per person per period, whether the period covers an address, a concession card, a medical assessment, an income record or a payment component, so this column and its start-date partner are what make DOMINO longitudinal rather than a set of snapshots.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 394, 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. Whether a still-open episode is left blank or carried with a sentinel far-future date varies between DOMINO tables, so check a column's maximum value before filtering on it.
limitation: The date closes an administrative record, not the circumstance behind it: an address period ends when the department was told of a change, not when the person moved, and a card period ends when the determination changed, not when the person stopped using the card. Periods on the same table can also abut or overlap after a retrospective correction, so counting rows is not the same as counting spells.
rationale: The registry maps period_end_date on the DOMINO distributions, including loc_dtls, ccd_hcc, mcd_dtls, inc_shc and the payment history tables, to the single data element 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD', which publishes its definition and date domain.
evidence_quote: The date on which a reporting period relating to an event ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Event end date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which said nothing about DOMINO's episode structure or about how open periods are represented.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 393, 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the record on this row starts applying. The DSS registry defines it as "The date on which a reporting period relating to an event commences, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". Every DOMINO table that holds history is keyed on a person and this date, so to use any of them you filter the pair of period columns against a date of interest; without them a table is a stack of overlapping records with no time dimension. On tables such as loc_dtls and ccd_hcc one person has many rows, and the start dates are what put them in order.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 393, 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain.
limitation: The start date is when the department recorded a circumstance as taking effect, not when it happened. A backdated grant carries an effective date earlier than the decision, and a late-reported address change carries one later than the move, so the column cannot be used to time real-world events precisely. It also marks the start of this record only, not of the person's dealings with the department.
rationale: The registry maps period_start_date across the DOMINO distributions to the single data element 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD', which publishes its definition and its ten-character date domain.
evidence_quote: The date on which a reporting period relating to an event commences, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Event start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing on the gap between an administrative effective date and the event it stands for.
