value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 174, 'Address: Australian postcode, Code'
variable_description: The postcode of the address Centrelink held for the person during this period. The DSS registry defines it as "The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area for an address". On the location details table it is the coarse end of a set of geography columns that runs from MESHBLOCK up through SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE to STATE, and it is the one taken straight off the reported address rather than derived by geocoding, so it survives where MESHMATCH shows the address never matched. The same column repeats on snap_domino_beta and on the temporary and terminated address table.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 174, 'Address: Australian postcode, Code'
value_definition: A four-digit code in the registry's Australian postcode code domain, which is Australia Post's set of postal delivery areas rather than an ABS statistical geography.
limitation: Postcodes are delivery areas, not statistical areas: a few cross state borders, some cover only post office boxes with no residents, and they do not nest inside SA2s or LGAs. Aggregating recipient counts by postcode and dividing by ABS regional populations therefore mismatches at the edges, and SA2_MAINCODE is the column to use instead.
rationale: The LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps postcode to 'Address: Australian postcode, Code', which publishes the definition and names the Australia Post derived value domain.
evidence_quote: The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area for an address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address postcode' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without warning that a postal geography does not align with ABS statistical areas.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108854, 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment'
variable_description: The income support payment the person was on immediately before the current one, within the same active payment spell. It is what lets a single snapshot row show a pathway rather than a state: a DSP row with JSP behind it is a successful disability claim, and a JSP row with PPS behind it is usually a single parent whose youngest child aged out of Parenting Payment Single. NEXT_ISP is the forward-looking partner, and FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP names where the spell began.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108854, 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment'
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which covers about a hundred payments: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS for Parenting Payment Single.
limitation: The previous payment is scoped to the current spell, so a person's earlier history before a long break is not visible here and the field is simply empty at the start of a spell. It also gives no date and no reason for the change, so it cannot distinguish a voluntary transfer from an automatic one such as the transfer of single parents onto JobSeeker Payment when a child reached the age cut-off.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.prev_isp to 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment' with the DSS benefit type code domain. That the field is empty at the start of a spell follows from the definition's scoping to the period of activity rather than being stated.
evidence_quote: Refers to the previous Income Support Payment type benefit (in this period of activity)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the code set or explaining that the lookback stops at the spell boundary.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 110042, 'Person: Principal Carer Indicator, Code X'
variable_description: Says whether the person was treated as the principal carer of a dependent child under 16 on the snapshot date. Principal carer status is what triggers the parenting payment rules, the reduced participation requirements and the higher single rate that apply to sole parents, so it explains rate differences that ISP_TYPE_CODE alone cannot. PRI_CARER_TOTAL_CHILDREN counts the qualifying children and PRI_CARER_AGE_YOUNGEST_CHILD gives the age of the youngest, which is the number most of the payment rules actually turn on.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 110042, 'Person: Principal Carer Indicator, Code X'
value_definition: One character, Y or N, with N as the registry's default, so a person with no qualifying children reads as N rather than as missing.
limitation: It is a payment status, not a statement of who lives with a child: care can be shared, and the parent who does not hold the status still cares for the child, so counting Y values undercounts parents. The under-16 test also means a parent supporting a 16-year-old reads as N while still carrying the cost.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.pri_carer to 'Person: Principal Carer Indicator, Code X' and publishes the Y and N permissible values with N as the default.
evidence_quote: The code that indicates whether a person is considered to have primary care of a dependent child under the age of 16 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the two-value domain nor the shared-care ambiguity was recorded.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 69050, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Youngest Child Age, Number'
variable_description: The age of the youngest child in the principal carer's care on the snapshot date, which is the number most parenting payment rules turn on. Parenting Payment Single ends when the youngest child reaches a set age, under eight until 20 September 2023 and under 14 from that date, and part-time participation requirements begin earlier, so this column explains transitions between payments that the payment type alone makes look arbitrary. It is only meaningful where PRI_CARER is Y.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 69050, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Youngest Child Age, Number'
value_definition: An integer age in whole years, held in the registry's Count N(8) domain. It refers to the youngest of the children counted by PRI_CARER_TOTAL_CHILDREN, not to all children in the household.
limitation: The value is an age at one date, so it cannot be used to date a birth or to identify the child, and successive snapshots of the same person can skip a year where a child enters or leaves care. Because the count behind it is payment scoped, a younger child who fails a residence or dependency test is ignored and the age recorded can be older than the youngest child actually present.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.pri_carer_age_youngest_child to 'Recipient: Principal Carer Youngest Child Age, Number' and publishes its Count N(8) domain. The Parenting Payment Single age cut-offs come from the 2023 legislative change that lifted the youngest child age from eight to 14.
evidence_quote: The age of the youngest child in the care of the Principal Carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without connecting the age to the payment thresholds that make it worth having.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 66073, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Children in Care Count, Total'
variable_description: Counts the children the person was responsible for on the snapshot date who met the dependency tests for a payment. It is a payment-scoped count and not a count of a person's children: the DSS registry defines it as the total of young people who meet "age, residence, income, study or job seeking or other dependency requirements for a particular payment, benefit or service". Read it with PRI_CARER, which says whether the person held principal carer status at all, and with CARD_ANY_MAX_CHILD_LISTED, which counts children listed on concession cards instead.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 66073, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Children in Care Count, Total'
value_definition: An integer count in the registry's Count N(8) domain. Zero appears for a person with no qualifying children.
limitation: A child who fails a residence, study or income test is invisible here, so the count can be lower than the number of children living in the home and should not be used as a family size measure. It is also not a fertility measure: children who have aged out of dependency drop out of the count, so the number falls over a parent's life while the number of children born to them does not.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.pri_carer_total_children to 'Recipient: Principal Carer Children in Care Count, Total', whose published definition names the dependency tests that scope the count, and gives the Count N(8) domain.
evidence_quote: The total count of young people for whom a customer has responsibility and who meets age, residence, income, study or job seeking or other dependency requirements for a particular payment, benefit or service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the difference between a payment-scoped count and the number of children in a family was never stated.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54748, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Indicator, Code'
variable_description: Marks a period during which the person was recorded as the principal carer of a dependent child, on the customer information table that holds principal carer history. Unlike the snapshot version of the same status in snap_domino_beta, this is an episode: PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the spell, so a person's principal carer history can be rebuilt and matched against their payment history. NSPP_PRCPL_CARER_RSN_CODE on the same row records the reason the status was granted.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54748, 'Recipient: Principal Carer Indicator, Code'
value_definition: One character. The registry's value domain is a yes-or-missing code: Y means the status applied, and there is no N, so an absent value means only that no principal carer status was recorded.
limitation: Because the domain has no N, the column cannot distinguish a person assessed as not a principal carer from a person never assessed, and inferring the negative from an absent row conflates the two. The flag also does not identify the child, so it cannot be joined to a particular dependant or used to count children.
rationale: The CIR_PRIN_CAR_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps principal_parent_ind to 'Recipient: Principal Carer Indicator, Code', whose value domain publishes Y as the only permissible value with a missing supplementary value.
evidence_quote: Principal Carer indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Principal carer indicator' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding that the domain carries no explicit negative value.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 84497, 'Payment: History Source, Code XXX'
variable_description: Says how the payment component on this row arose: as a regular recurring payment, as a one-off, or as an amount paid through a third party. It separates the fortnightly benefit stream from lump sums such as economic support payments and from money paid to someone else on the person's behalf, so summing CMPNT_DLY_AMT without filtering on it adds three different kinds of money together. The column appears on all twenty payment history tables, one per payment group, of which pyh_combined_dis is the disability and carers group.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 84497, 'Payment: History Source, Code XXX'
value_definition: A three-character code with three permissible values in the DSS registry: REG for regular, ONE for one-off and THP for third party.
limitation: The code describes how a payment was made, not what it was for: BEN_TYPE names the benefit and CMPNT_TYPE names the component, and a one-off supplement attached to a regular pension still reads as ONE. It also does not identify the third party in a THP row, so payments to a nominee, a landlord under rent deduction, or a service provider cannot be told apart here.
rationale: The PYH_COMBINED_DIS (PLIDA) distribution maps pyh_source to 'Payment: History Source, Code XXX', whose value domain publishes exactly three codes with their meanings. The data element's own definition describes the table rather than the column, so the description is written rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Longitudinal history of Centrelink reported payment's.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Payment source' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the domain has three values and mixing them corrupts any total of payment amounts.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108838, 'Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT on Snap'
variable_description: Says whether the person was receiving Rent Assistance on the snapshot date. Rent Assistance is not a payment in its own right but a supplement added to an income support payment or to Family Tax Benefit Part A, so this flag marks private renters among recipients and is the closest thing the snapshot table has to a housing indicator. RENT_TYPE_CODE, RENT_BEN_STATUS and RENT_PANEL_DAYS qualify it, and a Y here will normally sit beside a Y on ISP_ON_SNAP or FTBA_ON_SNAP because the supplement rides on a primary payment.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108838, 'Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT on Snap'
value_definition: One character, Y or N, from the DSS yes/no/missing code domain.
limitation: It marks receipt of a supplement, not renting. A recipient who pays rent to a state or territory housing authority is not eligible for Rent Assistance and reads as N despite paying rent, as does anyone whose rent falls below the minimum threshold or who has no formal liability in a share house. The flag also gives no rent paid, no dwelling type and no landlord.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.rent_on_snap to 'Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT on Snap' and publishes the Y and N values in the yes/no/missing domain. The public housing exclusion is a standing feature of Rent Assistance eligibility.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating rent assistance received on snap date
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning against reading the flag as a renter indicator.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108839, 'Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Panel Days'
variable_description: Counts the days the person received Rent Assistance across the panel window the snapshot belongs to, rather than on the snapshot day. It distinguishes sustained assistance from a short spell, which the RENT_ON_SNAP flag cannot. Because Rent Assistance attaches to a primary payment, a drop in this count usually reflects the primary payment ending rather than a change of housing, so it should be read against ISP_PANEL_DAYS and FTBA_PANEL_DAYS.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108839, 'Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Panel Days'
value_definition: An integer count of days in the registry's Count N(8) domain.
limitation: Days on Rent Assistance are not days spent renting, and the count cannot be converted into an amount: the daily rate depends on rent paid, family size and partner status, none of which appear on this table. A zero also covers both a person who rented without qualifying and a person who never rented.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.rent_panel_days to 'Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Panel Days' and publishes its Count N(8) domain.
evidence_quote: Number of days active on rent assistance.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing on why the count moves with the primary payment.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108892, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA1 main code, Code'
variable_description: The SA1 the person's address fell in, on the derived location table that holds one row per address episode. The ABS designs SA1s, in the registry's words, "to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data", which makes this the level at which a DOMINO record can be joined to Census small-area counts or to SEIFA. MB_ASGS_2021 on the same row is finer, SA2_ASGS_2021 and SA4_ASGS_2021 coarser, ARID_HASH_TRUNC identifies the address itself, and START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108892, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA1 main code, Code'
value_definition: An eleven-character ASGS 2021 SA1 code. SA1s are built from whole mesh blocks and aggregate to whole SA2s, so the geography columns on the row nest exactly and never contradict each other.
limitation: An SA1 holds roughly 200 to 800 people, so it is a neighbourhood rather than a household and a shared code is not evidence of co-residence. SA1 boundaries are also redrawn between ASGS editions, so codes cannot be compared across editions without a correspondence, and the edition of other SA1 columns in DOMINO should be checked before joining because the PLIDA data item list and the DSS registry disagree on some of them.
rationale: The LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA) distribution maps sa1_asgs_2021 to the ASGS 2021 SA1 main code data element, which publishes the ABS definition and the X(11) value domain.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) are geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks. Whole SA1s aggregate to form Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s). SA1s are designed to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data, represented as a code

variable_description: The SA2 of the person's address on the snapshot date. SA2 is the level most published ABS regional output uses, so this is the practical join between Snap DOMINO recipient counts and Census, SEIFA or regional population data, and the level at which a rate of income support receipt per head of population can be built. SA3, SA4, LGA, CED, GCCSA and POSTCODE on the same row are the same address at other levels, and MESHBLOCK is the finest.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108679, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA2 main code, Code'
value_definition: An ASGS 2021 SA2 code. The registry records the value domain with a four-digit format, which is shorter than the ABS nine-digit SA2 main code, so check the width of the column in the extract before joining to a boundary file.
limitation: An SA2 is designed to approximate a community of interest, not an administrative area, so it does not line up with the LGA or the Commonwealth electoral division on the same row and totals will not reconcile across them. It is also the address on file rather than where the person spends their time, so it cannot support claims about where services were used.
rationale: The SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps sa2 to the ASGS 2021 SA2 main code data element, whose published definition is the wording carried in the PLIDA data item list, and which names the 2021 SA2 value domain.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 499, 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency'
variable_description: The deemed income counted against the person for the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card income test in this reporting period. The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual deemed income a recipient receives", and deemed income is not money actually received but the return the deeming rules assume a person's financial assets, including account-based income streams, produce at set rates. It sits with SHC_AN_INC_TXB, SHC_AN_INC_FGN, SHC_AN_PRP_LOS, SHC_AN_EMP_BEN and SHC_AN_SAL_SCF, which together make up the adjusted taxable income the card is tested on, and PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the year it covers.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 499, 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency'
value_definition: An amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN, covering one year. It is a figure calculated from the deeming rates rather than a reported one.
limitation: It is not investment income actually received, so it cannot measure returns: two people with identical balances carry identical deemed income however their investments performed, and a year of losses still produces a positive number. It also reaches only the assets the deeming rules cover, so it is not a measure of a person's wealth.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_dmd_inc to 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency', which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain, and the same distribution shows the other income components tested for the card.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual deemed income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual deemed income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without explaining that deemed income is assumed rather than received.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 498, 'Recipient: Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits income, Total Australian currency'
variable_description: Employer-provided benefits the person received that do not appear in taxable income, added back for the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card income test. The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual employer-provided benefits a recipient receives, not included in taxable income". The column exists because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income rather than taxable income, so the amounts a tax return leaves out are collected separately here alongside SHC_AN_SAL_SCF for salary sacrifice, SHC_AN_INC_FGN for foreign income and SHC_AN_PRP_LOS for net investment and property losses.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 498, 'Recipient: Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits income, Total Australian currency'
value_definition: An annual amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN. It is zero for anyone with no employer, which is most card holders, since the card is aimed at people of Age Pension age.
limitation: It captures reportable fringe benefits for one income test, so it is not a measure of total remuneration and does not include compulsory employer superannuation contributions. A zero cannot be read as no employment either, only as no reportable benefits, so it is not a proxy for retirement.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_emp_ben to the Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits data element, which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual employer-provided benefits a recipient receives, not included in taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual employer provided benefits income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why an income test needs amounts left out of taxable income.

The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual foreign income a recipient receives". It is collected because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income, so a retiree living on an overseas pension is tested on that income even where it does not appear on an Australian tax return, and SHC_AN_INC_TXB on the same row holds the domestic taxable amount.
description_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 501, 'Recipient: Annual foreign income, Total Australian currency'

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: The taxable income Centrelink held for a person when testing them for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which DSS defines as "The amount of annual taxable income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). The inc_shc table carries one row per annual reporting period, bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, for people whose card eligibility was assessed. This column is one of seven income components on the row: deemed income, foreign income, employer provided benefits, net property and investment losses and salary sacrificed income sit beside it and are added to it to reach the adjusted taxable income the card is tested against. It answers what the card decision was based on, not what the person earned in total.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: A dollar amount for a whole year, unlike DOMINO's other income tables which hold a daily rate. The figure is what was reported to or held by Centrelink for the card assessment, and the external release applies variable rounding to the amount so that a person cannot be recognised from an unusual value.
limitation: It is not the person's ATO assessment. Centrelink records the taxable income relevant to the card test at the time of the test, so it can predate, lag or differ from the assessed figure in the ATO products in PLIDA, and it is only present for people whose seniors card eligibility was assessed rather than for all older Australians. Reading it as household income is also wrong: a couple is tested on combined income, but this row belongs to one person.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents inc_shc_ext as the longitudinal history of annually reported Centrelink income tied to seniors health card eligibility, and gives each column of the table its own definition, including this one.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual taxable income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's label 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual taxable income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing said what the figure was for or how it related to the six income columns beside it.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: An estimate of a year's taxable income used for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card assessment where an assessed figure was not available, defined by DSS as "The amount of annual estimated taxable income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). It sits directly beside SHC_AN_INC_TXB on the same annual row, which is the assessed rather than the estimated amount. Estimates arise when someone claims the card before a tax assessment exists for the relevant year, typically at retirement or on a first claim. The pair together shows whether the card decision rested on an estimate or on a settled figure.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: A dollar amount for a whole year, on the same footing as the assessed taxable income column and subject to the same variable rounding in the external release. It records what was estimated at the time of the assessment, not a revised figure.
limitation: The column cannot tell you which figure decided entitlement, nor whether the estimate was later replaced once a tax assessment issued. An estimate present alongside an assessed amount is not evidence of a dispute or of ineligibility, and the difference between the two is not an error measure: they can refer to different income years.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines every column of inc_shc_ext, including the estimated taxable income field, and describes the table as the annual Centrelink income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual estimated taxable income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell an estimate from the assessed amount held in the next column.

value_domain: Annual loss amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: The investment and rental property losses added back when a person's income is tested for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which DSS defines as "The amount of annual property and net investment losses a recipient incurs" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). Losses are added back because they reduce taxable income without reducing a person's capacity to support themselves, so the adjusted taxable income used for the card is higher than the taxable income beside it. A non-zero value here therefore raises the tested income rather than lowering it.

limitation: The column does not separate a negatively geared rental property from a geared share portfolio, so it cannot be used to identify property investors. It also says nothing about the asset behind the loss, which is tested separately under the assets test and is not carried in this table, and the sign convention is not published, so check the direction of the values before adding them to taxable income.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry gives this column its own definition inside the inc_shc_ext distribution, which it documents as the annual income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual property and net investment losses a recipient incurs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label 'annual net investment/property loss' and used one generic sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so it never explained that a loss increases the income the card is tested on.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: Income a person gave up under a salary sacrifice arrangement, counted back into the income test for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card and defined by DSS as "The amount of annual salary sacrificed income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). Like the property and investment loss column beside it, it is added back because sacrificing salary lowers taxable income without lowering the resources available to the person. For a card cohort at or near Age Pension age it usually reflects reportable contributions to superannuation made in the last working years.

rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_shc_ext, the distribution it documents as the annual Centrelink income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual salary sacrificed income a recipient receives.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: The day the Snap-DOMINO row describes, defined by DSS as "A primary reference date for derived items in Snap-Domino, recorded as a day of a month of a year, and represented as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). Everything else on the row is measured as at that day: the on-snap flags for income support, family payments, rent assistance and supplementary payments, the concession cards held, the address and its geography, age, partnered status and principal carer status. Snap-DOMINO exists so that a cross-section can be taken without assembling episodes from the underlying event tables, so this column, with the person key, is what makes a row unique.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, taking one of the fixed reference days on which the snapshot is cut rather than any day a person had a dealing with the agency.
limitation: It marks a chosen observation day, so anything that started and ended between two snapshot days is invisible: a short spell on a payment, a card that lapsed and was reissued, or a move and a move back. Rates built from Snap-DOMINO are point-in-time prevalence, not incidence, and comparing two snap dates measures stocks rather than flows.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT as snapshot views of individuals' interactions with the welfare system on specified days of the year, and defines this column as the reference date those derived items hang off.
evidence_quote: A primary reference date for derived items in Snap-Domino, recorded as a day of a month of a year, and represented as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's wording and then said only that no finite value list applies, twice, so nothing explained that every other column on the row is measured as at this date.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
variable_description: The day an address became the recipient's effective address in Centrelink's records, opening the location episode the rest of the row describes. The loc_derived table holds one row per episode: the hashed address register identifier, the address type and priority, and the mesh block, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state codings of that address under ASGS 2021. Read with END_DATE it gives a residential history assembled from welfare administration rather than from a survey, and ADDR_PRTY exists because a person can hold more than one open address at once.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, as every date column in DOMINO's location distributions is.
limitation: It dates a record, not a removal van. The address becomes effective when the person tells the agency or the agency updates its records, so a start date can trail a move by weeks or months and a person who stops dealing with Centrelink keeps an address that is no longer theirs. Episodes across address types can also overlap, so a start date here does not close the previous episode.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents the loc_derived distribution as derived location boundaries and lists its contents: the anonymised address register identifier, the address priority code, the address type and the ASGS 2021 geography, with dates carried in YYYY-MM-DD form. The registry does not publish this column under the PLIDA name START_DATE, so the shape is sourced and the reading of the date as the start of the address episode is written from the table's contents.
evidence_quote: Derived code highlighting address priority for identifying the location of a recipient on a given day.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Effective address start date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say what the episode was, what closed it, or why more than one address can be open at once.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution loc_dtls_ext
variable_description: The state or territory of the address held for the person, defined by DSS as "The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, loc_dtls_ext). Which address that is depends on the table: loc_dtls holds home addresses, loc_pos_temp_term_dtls holds postal, temporary and term addresses, and snap_domino_beta holds the address as at the snapshot day. On the location tables the column sits with POSTCODE, MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE for the same address, so it is the coarsest of several geographies for one place rather than a separate fact.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution loc_dtls_ext
value_definition: A short character code rather than a name: the registry gives the column as a character string of up to three characters, so the values are the usual state and territory abbreviations rather than numbers. Snap-DOMINO's STATE_CODE, by contrast, is a one-digit numeric code, so the two columns cannot be compared without recoding.
limitation: The state belongs to an address on file, not to a person, so a stale record puts someone in the state they left. On the postal and temporary address table the value can be a mailing state or a term address for a student, which is not where the person lives, and MESHMATCH warns that the finer geography beside it may have been matched from coordinates rather than from the address itself.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines loc_dtls_ext as the location of an individual's home addresses in DOMINO and gives this column its own definition; the companion distribution loc_pos_temp_term_dtls_ext, documented as non-home addresses, carries the same column.

description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)

It also says nothing about where a payment was administered or assessed, so it should not be used as a service-delivery region, and an address that could not be geocoded contributes no code at all rather than an unknown-state code.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents the loc_derived distribution and defines this column as the state or territory of an address represented by a code; the ASGS single-digit state and territory codes are the ABS standard the 2021 suffix names.

variable_description: The person key every DOMINO table is joined on, described by DSS as "A synthetic numeric sequence of characters used for the purposes of identifying a unique DOMINO entity" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, CCD_HCC_EXT). One value ties a person's payment history, income, concession cards, addresses, relationships, education and medical assessments together across the sixty-odd tables that carry it, which is what makes DOMINO a longitudinal record rather than a set of extracts. Within PLIDA the same key runs across products: MBS, PBS, the tax products, Census and the rest carry SYNTHETIC_AEUID under the same custodian description, Synthetic MADIP Person ID, so a DOMINO row joins to another agency's row on this column directly rather than through a separate mapping file.

A person absent from DOMINO is a person with no dealings with the department rather than a person with no need, and a person who fails to join to another PLIDA product has no record there rather than no history: the key is only as complete as the linkage behind it.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry gives the column its definition on every DOMINO distribution released to PLIDA, including the health care card determination table this occurrence sits in, and the PLIDA data item list names it as the synthetic MADIP person identifier held against the agency spine.

The mcd_dtls table is the record of medical conditions and work capacity assessments behind disability and participation decisions, holding the primary and secondary condition codes, an impairment rating, and the assessed hours a person can work. It marks when an assessor accepted that a condition limits what the person can do for a bounded time, which is the distinction that separates a temporary exemption from participation requirements from a continuing incapacity. INCAP_START and INCAP_END on the same row hold incapacity periods, and IMPRMT_CODE and IMPRMT_RATE hold the impairment that was rated.

It is therefore a poor measure of when ill health began, and comparing it with a medical event date in the health products will overstate any delay attributed to the person.

Reduced capacity is the milder of the two temporary findings on this table: limited capacity suspends what a person can be asked to do, while reduced capacity cuts the hours, and TEMP_REDN_CAP_HRS_NUM holds the size of that cut. Reading the two together shows whether an assessment stopped or merely trimmed a person's participation obligations.

evidence_quote: The date on which a period of temporary reduction in capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary reduced capacity end date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither separated reduced from limited capacity nor warned that no start date exists for this period.

It is a change, not a level: CURR_CAPCTY_NUM on the same row holds the current assessed capacity in hours a week and WITH_INTRVN_NUM holds the capacity with intervention, so this column has to be read against them to say what the person was assessed as able to do. Weekly hours are the currency of these decisions because payment and participation rules turn on hour thresholds rather than on a diagnosis.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A whole number of hours in a week, recorded against the assessment that made the finding.
limitation: Assessed hours are not worked hours. Nothing here records whether the person had a job, and actual earnings sit in the employment income tables, so the column cannot be used to measure labour supply. Because the value is a reduction, treating it as remaining capacity inverts its meaning.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside mcd_dtls_ext, alongside the current capacity and with-intervention hour columns that give it its scale.
evidence_quote: The number of reduction in hours a recipient is able to work in a week
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary reduced capacity hours number' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say the number is a reduction rather than a capacity, which is the error a reader would otherwise make.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext
variable_description: Whether the person being cared for has a terminal illness, defined by DSS as an "Indicator that a caree has a terminal illness" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_caree_ext). The mcd_caree table is medical information about care receivers, collected because someone claimed Carer Payment or Carer Allowance for them, so every column on the row describes the cared-for person while the person key on the row is the carer. A terminal illness matters administratively because it changes how a carer claim is assessed and how quickly it can be granted.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext
value_definition: A yes or no indicator recorded against a care receiver's medical record for the period the row covers.
limitation: The flag belongs to the care receiver, not to the person whose identifier is on the row, so reading it as the carer's own health inverts the record. It also reflects what was reported to support a claim, so it is not a clinical diagnosis, gives no prognosis or date, and its absence means only that nothing was recorded.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents mcd_caree_ext as the medical conditions of the caree for a recipient of Carer Payment or Carer Allowance, and defines this indicator directly.
evidence_quote: Indicator that a caree has a terminal illness.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Terminal illness indicator' with the value domain left as 'not specified' and the generic sentence in both fields, so it never said whose illness is being flagged.

Carer Payment and Carer Allowance claims turn on a medical report about the person being cared for, and this column is what distinguishes the doctor or specialist who completed one report from another. Rows sharing a value came from the same professional, which is the only clinician-level structure DOMINO carries.

rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside mcd_caree_ext and states explicitly that it is not a foreign key to an external provider file, which is the claim a reader most needs.
evidence_quote: Identifies which Treating Health Professional from which the data was supplied. It is not a foreign key to an external provider/third party file.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Treating health professional synthetic id' with an inferred opaque-identifier domain and the generic sentence twice, so it left open the join to MBS provider data that the source explicitly rules out.

variable_description: Compensation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the "Daily rate of continuous income from compensation received by a recipient" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). Recorded as documented record-level values rather than an exhaustive list: METEOR declares the value domain as a total number, and the three are what get summed to derive it.
evidence_quote: Number of services is derived by summing the possible values: +1 ... -1 ... 0
supersedes_rationale: Earlier record named no domain. Judgement call for the generator: it currently draws NUMSERV from 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities 0.95/0.03/0.01/0.01. That is not absurd, but it never produces the documented -1 cancellation and 0 adjustment records, and it produces values above 1 that the published guide does not describe at record level. If you change anything, add a small share of -1 and 0 records rather than widening the positive range.

value_domain: PLIDA synthetic person identifier (Agency Entity Unique ID)
value_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The patient a Medicare claim line belongs to, carried as a meaningless code so that one person's services can be followed across the date-of-service tables without a Medicare number. The Productivity Commission describes how the ABS builds it: "The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it". It is the only person-level key on the row, so grouping by it turns claim lines into a patient's service history, with BENPAID, FEECHARGED and NUMSERV summing per person and ITEM, BTOS and MBSCAT saying what was done. Different datasets from one data source carry consistent values, so the column joins the MBS tables to each other, but the Productivity Commission describes every dataset in the PLIDA Modular Product as joined through its own concordance table, so a join to PBS, AIR or any other dataset should be confirmed against those tables rather than assumed, and reaching Census, ATO or Centrelink data means going through the spine linkage file.
description_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque code standing in for the patient's Medicare enrolment identifier, repeated on every claim line for that person and held consistently across the tables from the same source. It follows no published classification and carries no age, sex, location or card information, so there is no finite list to publish and nothing in the value to decode or order.
limitation: The value cannot be matched against the identifier for the same person in another agency's data, because the Productivity Commission notes that "Synthetic AEUIDs are unique to an entity within a data source and are not repeated across sources": an MBS value equal to a Census or ATO value is a coincidence, not a person. It names the patient the service was for, not the person who lodged the claim or paid the account, and not the practitioner, who is SCRAM_SPR when servicing and SCRAM_RPR when referring. Whether the patient can be reached anywhere else in PLIDA depends on the separate spine linkage file, in which a record that did not match the spine carries no spine identifier at all.
rationale: The PLIDA data item list gives this field as the synthetic MADIP person ID on all 259 MBS date-of-service claims tables from 2006 to 2025, being 240 monthly tables and 19 annual supplementary tables, and the Productivity Commission's PLIDA guide documents what a Synthetic AEUID is, how the ABS creates it, that it is unique within one data source, and that concordance tables carry it to a Spine AEUID. The ABS names the column itself on its Labour Force Survey-PLIDA page, saying the survey's person identifier is replaced with an anonymised PLIDA person ID SYNTHETIC_AEUID, which confirms the same design applies column for column. That the MBS value is the patient rather than the provider comes from the columns beside it: SCRAM_SPR and SCRAM_RPR carry the providers, and the MBS note on ENRPC says the patient demographics on the row are sourced from the Medicare enrolment file at the time the claim was processed.
evidence_quote: The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's four words, 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID', with a domain of 'Opaque identifier (inferred)' guessed from the variable name and a value definition and limitation that both said only that the domain was inferred from the name and open. Nothing told a reader that the identifier is the patient rather than the provider, that it is minted per data source, or that a join to another PLIDA module has to go through the spine.

value_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: Whether the address on this row is where the person lives or where Medicare sends their mail. Medicare enrolment addresses are among the most current in the asset, because people deal with the system often, but only the residential ones can be read as a place of residence. The distinction matters most for children, who are enrolled on a parent's card and take that card's address.
description_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation
limitation: The domain is inferred from the variable name and its siblings in the other address tables, not from a published list, so the exact codes are not confirmed. A person with only a postal address on file has no residential row, which is a gap rather than an absence of residence.
rationale: The DIL describes the field as an address type on the Medicare enrolment address tables, matching the residential-or-postal field of the same name in ATO_CR, DOMINO and Core Locations. No published code list was found.
evidence_quote: Address type
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address type' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address held on the person's Medicare enrolment, for one period of their address history bounded by START_DATE and END_DATE. Medicare addresses update when a person deals with the system, which for children and for anyone with regular claims is often, so this is one of the more current address sources feeding Core Locations. ADR_TYP separates a residential address from a postal one and CNTRY_CDE carries the country where the address is overseas.
description_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. A Medicare address belongs to the enrolment, so children on a parent's card carry that parent's address whether or not they live there. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed address register id on the Medicare enrolments address tables, whose start and end dates bound the episode. ABS publishes what the Address Register identifier is, and documents Core Locations as combining source address histories of this shape.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'not specified' as its domain and the same generic sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_source: ABS PLIDA data and legislation

CNTRY_CDE on the same row carries an overseas country of residence, so a missing address type often means the address is not in Australia at all.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL describes the field as the type of address and gives residential and postal as its examples, matching the field of the same name in the ATO and Medicare address tables. No published code list was found.

variable_description: The year the visa holder was born. PLIDA does not carry a date of birth: the day is removed and the year and month are supplied separately, so age can be computed to within a month and never exactly. Age at arrival is one of the strongest predictors of migrant outcomes, and this is the year half of the only age measure the asset offers.

value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse data dictionary
variable_description: The kind of dwelling the care recipient usually lives in, recorded at assessment. It is the column that separates someone living in a private home from someone already in supported or residential accommodation, which is the difference between a home-support pathway and a residential one. Because it is captured at assessment it describes where the person was living when assessed, not where they went afterwards.
description_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse data dictionary
value_definition: A category naming the dwelling type. Private dwellings, retirement villages, supported residential services and residential aged care are the distinctions the assessment turns on.
limitation: The value is a snapshot at assessment and does not update when the person moves, so it cannot be used to track a transition into residential care; the care-type and service records do that. It describes the dwelling rather than the household, so it says nothing about whether the person lives alone, which the carer columns carry instead.
rationale: The AIHW data dictionary defines the accommodation attributes recorded against an aged care assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a one-line curated description with no value domain, so the page still said 'not specified' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence.

value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
variable_description: The day a resident took up a place of a particular type inside a residential aged care home. The AIHW data dictionary for this collection defines the element as one that "Identifies the date a person was admitted into care", and warns that "Moving from one type of place to another within the same service/facility will involve two records with differing admission dates". That is why rac_episode also carries ENTRY_DATE and EXIT_DATE: those two bracket a continuous stay in the service, while ADMISSION_DATE and DISCHARGE_DATE bracket a stay in one type of place within it. Read with ADMISSION_TYPE, it dates the start of a permanent stay or of a respite stay.
description_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
value_definition: A calendar date, held in the source system as DD/MM/YYYY. It is a claiming date drawn from the residential care payment system rather than a clinical record, so it is the day from which subsidy was payable for the place.
limitation: A second admission date for the same person and home is not proof of a second stay: a resident who converts from a respite place to a permanent place inside the same home gets a fresh row with no gap in care. The column also carries no waiting time, because the aged care assessment that approved the person sits on a different table with its own approval dates.
rationale: The NACDC data dictionary documents admission_date as a common data element of this collection, gives its definition and data domain, and explains the place-type behaviour that produces multiple admission rows for one continuous stay.
evidence_quote: Moving from one type of place to another within the same service/facility will involve two records with differing admission dates.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Date of admission of recipient to a place of a particular type in a service facility', and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: residential aged care admission type (permanent or respite)
value_source: AIHW GEN Aged Care Data, Glossary
variable_description: Whether the residential stay starting on this row was a permanent placement or a short respite stay. The AIHW GEN glossary draws the same line: "Admission to residential care can be long-term and on an ongoing basis (permanent residential care) or short-term on a planned or emergency basis (residential respite care)." The distinction governs almost everything else about the row, because respite stays are capped in days and permanent stays are not, and because the two are funded and means tested differently. The AIHW records that respite care is still offered at high and low care levels, while that split was removed for permanent care from 1 July 2014.
description_source: AIHW GEN Aged Care Data, Glossary
value_definition: A short text label separating permanent residential care from residential respite care. It restates the care type the place was approved for, which is the same distinction the Australian Government uses to set the subsidy and the fee rules for the stay.
limitation: It does not show a respite stay turning into a permanent one. A person who converts is given a separate row with its own admission date, so following one person needs the rows ordered rather than this column read alone. Nor does the column carry any respite day balance, so it cannot say whether a stay fell inside the 63 days of respite a person is entitled to in a financial year.
rationale: The GEN glossary, published by the AIHW alongside this data holding, defines residential care in exactly the permanent-or-respite terms the column encodes, and the NACDC data dictionary describes the same split in its account of the residential aged care collection.
evidence_quote: Admission to residential care can be long-term and on an ongoing basis (permanent residential care) or short-term on a planned or emergency basis (residential respite care).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's phrasing and the generic sentence saying no finite value list is published, printed twice.

value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
variable_description: The day an aged care assessment team decision stopped having effect, closing the eligibility that APPROVAL_START_DATE opened. The AIHW data dictionary covers both dates in one element, "The effective start date of approval for care (ACAP/ACCR) or funding (ACFI/RCS), and the effective end date for same". Most approvals end because a later reassessment replaced them rather than because the person stopped needing care, so the two dates together describe how long one particular decision stood.
description_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
value_definition: A calendar date in DD/MM/YYYY in the source system. The AIHW notes for the related effective-date element that an end date is frequently open-ended, and an open value marks a record that was still active.
limitation: A closed approval is not evidence that care ended or that the person was found ineligible. It is also not a waiting time: a person can hold a live approval for years without entering care, so the interval between the two approval dates measures the life of a decision, not the length of any service episode.
rationale: The NACDC data dictionary documents the effective start and end dates of approval for care as one common data element, and separately notes that end dates are commonly left open while a record is active.
evidence_quote: End date is frequently open-ended and indicates the record is active.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'The date the approval decision ended.' and printed the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
variable_description: The day an aged care assessment team decision took effect, opening the person's eligibility for the care named on the same row. The AIHW data dictionary defines the paired element as "The effective start date of approval for care (ACAP/ACCR) or funding (ACFI/RCS), and the effective end date for same". It qualifies CARE_APPROVAL_TYPE and CARE_APPROVAL_LEVEL, which say what was approved, and sits before any entry date in hcp_episode, since approval and entry are separate steps handled by different parties.
description_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
value_definition: A calendar date in DD/MM/YYYY in the source system, taken from the assessment record rather than from a service provider. It dates the legal effect of the approval, which can differ from the day the assessment was conducted.
limitation: Approval is not care. The AIHW notes that the assessment programme only grants approval, that providers handle entry, and that a varying amount of time passes in between, so this date is a poor proxy for when support began and a gap to ENTRY_DATE measures queueing rather than need.
rationale: The NACDC data dictionary documents assessment_start_date and assessment_end_date as a single common data element covering the effective dates of an approval for care, which is what the home care assessment table holds.
evidence_quote: The effective start date of approval for care (ACAP/ACCR) or funding (ACFI/RCS), and the effective end date for same.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'The date the approval decision started.' and carried the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: What the assistance recorded on this row cost to deliver. It is the provider's own reported cost rather than a price or a subsidy, so it measures what was spent on the service and not what the recipient paid or what government contributed. Read with ASSISTANCE_MINUTES_NBR and ASSISTANCE_QUANTITY_NBR it gives a cost per hour or per unit, which is the only way to compare service intensity across providers whose units differ.
description_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
value_definition: A dollar amount for the assistance on this row. Reporting requirements changed over the life of the programme, so an amount is only comparable within a reporting period.
limitation: Cost reporting is not audited and providers apply overheads differently, so a difference between providers can be an accounting difference rather than a real one. A zero or missing amount often means the cost was not reported rather than that the service was free.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the assistance attributes reported against a service delivery record in the Data Exchange, which is the collection this clearinghouse field is drawn from.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description 'Cost amount of assistance provided.' with no value domain, so the page repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: How long the assistance on this row took, in minutes. Minutes are the comparable unit across service types where quantity is not: an hour of domestic assistance and an hour of nursing are both sixty minutes, while their quantity counts mean different things. Not every service type reports minutes, so this column is populated for time-based services and empty for others.
description_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
value_definition: A count of minutes, not hours. Services delivered in a group setting report the recipient's own minutes rather than the session's length.
limitation: An empty value means minutes were not the reporting unit for that service type, not that no time was spent, so treating blanks as zero understates delivery. Minutes measure contact, not benefit, and a service delivered efficiently records fewer of them.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the assistance attributes reported against a service delivery record in the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description 'Number of minutes of assistance provided.' with no value domain.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
variable_description: How much assistance was delivered, counted in whatever unit that service type uses. The unit is not carried on this column, so a quantity is meaningless without the service type beside it: meals, trips, hours and visits all appear here as bare numbers. Comparing quantities across service types adds meals to trips.
description_source: DSS Data Exchange, Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols
value_definition: A count in the service type's own unit. The unit is fixed by the service type rather than recorded per row.
limitation: The column cannot be summed across service types, which is the mistake it invites, and it cannot be compared with ASSISTANCE_MINUTES_NBR because the two measure different things for the same service. A quantity of one can be a single meal or a full day of respite.
rationale: The Commonwealth Home Support Programme protocols define the assistance attributes reported against a service delivery record in the Data Exchange, with the unit of measure set by the service type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description 'Quantity of assistance provided.' with no value domain, and nothing warned that the unit varies by service type.

value_source: AIHW, National Aged Care Data Clearinghouse Data Dictionary, Version 1.0 (2016), cat. no. AGE 80
variable_description: The month of the year in which the care recipient was born, kept without the day. The aged care source systems hold a full date of birth, which the AIHW records as the basis for calculating age and as one of the fields used with sex and letters of name for statistical record linkage; what reaches this table is that date reduced to a month and a year so the person cannot be identified from it. Paired with BIRTH_YEAR it pins age to within a month at any admission, discharge or assessment date on the other tables.

Nor can it be used to confirm identity against another collection holding a full date of birth, since the day of the month is gone.
rationale: The NACDC data dictionary documents date of birth as a common data element of this collection, gives its use in age calculation and record linkage, and lists the tables it appears on. The reduction to month and year is a de-identification step rather than a published element, so the description is written rather than quoted.
